I discovered Bret Easton Ellis shortly after my 13th birthday, which is really the only time you should discover Bret Easton Ellis. He was the author of choice for prodigious brats and queers, a swishy nonsense nihilist who had, years earlier, appalled the literary establishment with novels about Wall Street sociopaths and ambisexual teen druggies. The horror and the allure of Ellis’s work was in their trim, colourless prose: Less Than Zero, The Rules of Attraction and American Psycho were tales of lurid sex and violence presented so flatly that they were almost mundane. “I look up, admiringly, at Trump Tower, tall, proudly gleaming in the late afternoon sunlight,” goes his poreless, proto-looksmaxxer serial killer Patrick Bateman. “In front of it two smartass n***** teenagers are ripping off tourists at three-card monte and I have to fight the impulse to blow them away.”

Ellis was dangerous and nasty, and so blithely unconcerned about his own controversy-stoking that he made teenage-me swoon. That said, I haven’t read or much thought about Bret Easton Ellis since those days. He is an eternally adolescent proposition, like Blue Banana or contraband WKDs in the park, which is probably why he’s fallen so aggressively out of favour. If the literati never particularly dug him, and his juvenile fandom grew up, who’s left? The stragglers picked up by Ellis’s lengthy post-Obama Twitter rants about wokeness and the “professionally aggrieved”? Do they even read books?

So it came as a surprise to see that Bret Easton Ellis had come out of purgatory, and bigger and better funded than he has been in years. The fault lies with Ryan Murphy, the discourse merchant behind everything from American Horror Story to The Beauty, who has adapted – with Ellis himself – the author’s schlocky, occasionally sincere 2023 autofiction slasher novel The Shards for television. It’s slightly mad that their paths haven’t crossed until now. Murphy is the closest thing TV has ever had to its own Bret Easton Ellis, a man who inspires as much guilty pleasure in his acolytes as he does opprobrium and confusion.

The Shards – which is streaming now on Disney+ – doesn’t really work as a TV show, because salacious exploits of the rich and shameless is basically all of television now, and because its young, vaporous cast, which includes the daughter of Cindy Crawford and the son of Richard Gere, are a bit too blank to effectively convey intentional blankness. They all just seem remarkably unskilled, and tedious to boot. But The Shards has the unforeseen effect of making Ellis’s source material actually look quite brilliant, even if you’d long consigned him to the clearance bin of popular culture.

open image in gallery Bret Easton Ellis in 2019 ( Getty )

Ellis was just 21 when Less Than Zero hit shelves in 1985, the media anointing him a figure of Holden Caulfield-esque generational alienation, and the product of a culture gone to seed. “This is one of the most disturbing novels I’ve read in a long time,” went The New York Times, which presumably made Ellis’s publishers very happy. His story of boozing and drugging Hollywood offspring became a bestseller, and was so convincingly lived-in that Ellis would repeatedly face claims that it was autobiographical. It wasn’t, but its louche yet chic sense of apathy was at least reared during his time at the elite Vermont school Bennington College, where his classmates included Donna Tartt. She’d go on to write every moody alt-girl’s favourite novel The Secret History.

Less Than Zero is disturbing at junctures, particularly a scene of rape that chilled me even at my edgelord-iest, but it’s otherwise written so languorously – bored, even – that it almost becomes silly. Ellis termed it a satire, and you’re inclined to believe him. Everything is described with such ironic detachment, whether it’s anorexia, plastic surgery, drug abuse or murder, that it’s all ultimately meaningless. He swam in similar waters for its follow-up, 1987’s The Rules of Attraction, which shifted focus out of high school and into an elite liberal arts college, to lesser effect.

American Psycho, released when Ellis was 26, took ironic detachment to near-fatal extremes. It remains Ellis’s funniest novel (see the chapter on the existential brilliance of Whitney Houston), and his most purely ugly – the descriptions of some of the acts that yuppie investment banker and serial killer Bateman inflicts on women are objectively vile, and haven’t been neutered by time. American Psycho was binned by its original publishers and banned for sale to under-18s in numerous countries. For years it carried such a toxic reputation that feminist activist Gloria Steinem personally pushed Leonardo DiCaprio to drop out of its film adaptation for the sake of his young female fanbase.

While American Psycho itself has gone gloriously mainstream since its 1991 publication (there’s even been a musical, for goodness sake), it’s debatable whether Ellis’s own career properly recovered. The Informers, a collection of gonzo LA short stories released in 1994, and 1998’s Glamorama both veer into slight Bret Easton Ellis pastiche, like a photocopy of a photocopy. Glamorama in particular is like Less Than Zero gone berserk, railroaded with celebrity references, brand names and fashion labels, then inexplicable ruminations on state surveillance and terrorism.

open image in gallery ‘Less Than Zero’, ‘American Psycho’ and ‘The Shards’ are among Ellis’s best-known works ( Simon & Schuster/Vintage/Alfred A Knopf/Adobe )

Ellis seemed to go further adrift in the Noughties, first by lambasting Mary Harron’s sterling adaptation of American Psycho starring Christian Bale – which was coolly received upon release but has aged like fine wine – and releasing two lightly metatextual novels that lacked his earlier bite. There was 2005’s Lunar Park, in which “Bret Easton Ellis”, a slumming novelist, moves to the suburbs and experiences both literal and psychological hauntings. It was dubbed “the portrait of a narcissist who is terminally bored with himself” by The New York Times. Then he wrote a Less Than Zero sequel, 2010’s limp Imperial Bedrooms, before becoming a professional old man yelling at a cloud on Twitter, venting his feelings on the state of the world.

Then came White, a collection of moany essays published in 2019, which lifted wholesale many of the circular arguments Ellis was already having on Twitter at the time. He’d complain about Moonlight winning the Oscar, how it’s sad that people can’t joke about HIV any more, and why the liberal media was wrong to worry about Donald Trump’s presidency. A sensationally dismal interview in The New Yorker to promote White, in which he dodged or expressed chronic disinterest in discussing any of the political stances he wrote a whole book about, seemed to be the nail in his coffin.

It’s possible that the decline of Twitter helped us all forget those years when Ellis became unbearable, or that Bateman’s hilarious infatuation with Trump in American Psycho (he repeatedly invokes him as the pinnacle of style and taste) inspired many to take a second, more forgiving look at his masterpiece.

But I’m more inclined to believe it’s to do with what’s trendy right now. Ellis’s spare, dishy tales of Los Angeles ennui aren’t worlds away from the spare, dishy tales of Los Angeles ennui by Joan Didion and Eve Babitz (only with, you know, more chainsaws and violence), both of whom have experienced a resurgence among young readers in recent years. A boom in fast, fragmentary fiction – dubbed “Adderall novels” by the Los Angeles Times in April – couldn’t have harmed him any, either.

open image in gallery Bret (Igby Rigney), Debbie (Hayes Warner) and Robert (Homer Gere) in the new TV adaptation of ‘The Shards’ ( FX/Disney )

And he’s also, when he’s at his best, just shockingly good. Rereading Less Than Zero and American Psycho this week, I was struck by how funny his novels are, how immersive and strange they tend to be. They read like an uninterrupted broadcast of MTV in its heyday, where expensive pop music would pivot to loud s selling you a lifestyle you didn’t need, all the while the world around you burns. They read like America, in all its dazzle and madness, and how appealing that all is when you’re at an age where you’re still finding yourself. I was reminded of the fact that legendary girl-about-town Peaches Geldof created a very short-lived magazine called Disappear Here in 2008, inspired by a recurring phrase in Less Than Zero that seems to follow around its hero, and how fitting it was that Peaches Geldof – lost, anarchic, exhausting – was a Bret Easton Ellis devotee. And how sad it is that she’s long dead.

I began to think about how important it is to dip a toe in that sort of danger as a teenager, if only to teach you what absolutely not to do once you get your life together. And it may be the silver lining of a show as banal as The Shards. Someone out there will hopefully read the novels that inspired it, be horrified and intrigued, and make them their whole personality for a while. Then they’ll turn 14 and (hopefully) outgrow him, but still remember his work with a cringey fondness. It’s a chequered legacy, sure, but a legacy all the same.

‘The Shards’ is streaming on Disney+

A schoolgirl died from critical wounds on Saturday after a student opened fire at a high school and his home outside Bangkok the day before, bringing the death toll from the attack to at least eight people.

The 14-year-old opened fire at around 10 am Friday at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province northwest of the Thai capital before apparently taking his own life.

He also appeared to have killed his two grandparents at his family home earlier in the morning, officials said.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

The girl, 12, died after hospitalisation, the Health Ministry said. The school had posted a message on Facebook Friday seeking blood donations for two students, including the girl, who was in seventh grade.

Fourteen people remain hospitalised, of whom seven remain in critical condition Saturday, according to Thailand’s Health Ministry.

Most of those wounded were between 12 and 14 years old.Relatives claimed the bodies of eight people from Bangkok’s Institute of Forensic Medicine: five school staff, the accused shooter, and his grandparents.

Emergency workers brought out a coffin and loaded it onto an ambulance, which will transport the bodies to their hometowns for funeral rites.

The young girl’s body is still to be released.

Wiroon Supasingsiripreecha, head of the institute, said most of the victims suffered a single fatal gunshot wound to a vital area, including the chest or head.

He said the gunshot wound found on the alleged shooter was consistent with the weapon he had used. More detailed forensic findings, including toxicology results, are expected later, he said.

Officials said the gun, described as small and compact, was legally registered to the boy’s grandfather.

There were reports that the boy, who lived with his grandparents, had shown signs of stress connected to school, although some of his relatives told Thai media that they were unaware of any troubles he might have been facing.

The co-educational state school, which has about 3,000 students enrolled aged 12 to 18, said all classes would be suspended between Aug 10-14 and school staff were instructed to work from home during that time.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

A few mourners laid flowers Saturday morning at the school's gate, where a few police officers could be seen.

Charin Siriananchai brought his two sons, ages 9 and 6, to pay their respects.

He said while his sons do not study here, he lives in the neighbourhood and drives past this school almost every day, often stopping to allow students to cross the road.

“Everyone was saddened and shocked, because it was unexpected that this would happen in Thailand, and also it’s quite a great loss,” he said.

Some parents also came with their children to collect their belongings left behind after the shooting. A father, who declined to identify himself, said his son, who was at the school during the shooting, was still in shock and could not sleep alone.

Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in Asia, second only to Pakistan and far surpassing its Southeast Asian neighbours.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Data collected in 2017 by the groups Small Arms Survey and GunPolicy.org in their last extensive international study found civilian gun ownership in Thailand was about 15.1 guns per 100 people, compared with less than one per 100 in neighbouring Malaysia.

Thailand had 3.49 deaths by firearms per 100,000 people, according to 2023 statistics published by World Population Review.

That puts it well behind parts of Latin America and the Caribbean, but relatively high in Asia. Only the Philippines is higher in Southeast Asia.While shootings involving indiscriminate killings are not common, the country has seen an uptick in high-profile shooting deaths in recent years.

In February, a 17-year-old stole a gun from police and opened fire at a public high school in southern Thailand, briefly taking people hostage in a two-hour attack that killed one person and wounded two others.

A 14-year-old boy was accused of a 2023 shooting at a major Bangkok shopping mall.

When a shot rang out at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School on the outskirts of Bangkok on Friday morning, 14-year-old Khim and her classmates peered over a balcony to see if the noise had come from a construction site.

Trapped inside their classroom in Building 5, Khim started checking ‌messages on her tablet.

In the middle of her shift at a public hospital on Friday morning, 52-year-old nurse Kwan said she received a panicked call from her older daughter - Khim's sibling - to tell her of a shooting at their school.

open image in gallery Flowers and pictures of teachers killed are left outside Debsirin Nonthaburi School following a deadly shooting at the school, in Bang Kruai district in Nonthaburi province, on the outskirts of Bangkok, Thailand, August 9, 2026. REUTERS/Valeria Mongelli ( Reuters )

But more loud bangs followed, until a teacher ushered them all into a classroom, checked a messaging group and confirmed to the now terrified students: there was an active shooter in their building.

"I heard multiple gunshots and felt like we weren't going to survive," Khim, who asked to be only identified by her nickname, told Reuters on Saturday, describing how her classmates moved desks to block a door, turned off the lights and huddled together near the classroom windows.

Over the next 40 minutes or so, the alleged gunman – another 14-year-old student – ran amok, killing three teachers and two school officials, before turning the gun on himself.

open image in gallery Khim, a 14-year-old eighth-grade student at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, shows footage she recorded during evacuation, during an exclusive interview with Reuters about what she saw and witnessed during the shooting incident at the school, a day after the incident, in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, on the outskirts of Bangkok, Thailand, August 8, 2026. REUTERS/Chalinee Thirasupa ( Reuters )

In all, nine people have ​been ⁠killed and another 23 wounded, in Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022, which has reignited debate over firearms control in Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation.

The tragedy had actually begun hours earlier, when the alleged gunman shot dead his grandparents at their home at dawn. He then took a bus to the school, 18km (11miles) away, where he pulled out a gun and started shooting just before 10am (0300GMT), police said.

Her elder sister wrote to say she was inside a classroom in Building 4 next door, just as their mother messaged to warn about the shooter.

"I said I knew, and I told her, 'Mom, don't call me, because the ringtone might go off,'" said Khim.

On student chat groups, some photographs of the alleged shooter started circulating as he stalked through the school, which has more than 3,000 students and nearly 150 teachers, according to data from last year.

open image in gallery Students arrive at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, a day after the shooting at the school, in Nonthaburi province, Thailand Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

"Then, I heard a bang that was extremely loud. It felt like it was right next to my ear," said Khim, describing the absolute terror that descended on the classroom as she realised that the gunman was only a few doors down the corridor.

"I didn't know if the shooter was shooting selectively. I didn't know if he wanted to shoot the whole school."

Not long after, Khim said the teacher issued instructions to evacuate the classroom, as police secured parts of the school – but by then, the shooter had moved to Building 4, where her sibling was still hiding.

Based on conversations on a student chat group that her elder daughter told her about, Kwan – who also asked to be identified by a nickname – said she assessed that the shooter was likely using a handgun.

Still on the phone, she asked her elder daughter to count the shots, estimating that a ‌handgun magazine wouldn't hold more than 15 to 20 rounds: "Count the shots to see if he's out."

Police said the alleged shooter had used at least 26 bullets. Another 34 rounds were found in his possession.

open image in gallery A family member of a teacher killed in a deadly shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, reacts as the body is received at Police General Hospital, in Bangkok, Thailand, August 8, 2026. REUTERS/Valeria Mongelli ( Reuters )

"But it turned out the sound kept getting closer and ‌closer, eventually reaching Building 4, the building my daughter was in," Kwan ⁠told Reuters on Saturday.

From another phone, she called an emergency hotline, on which the operator told her that police, including a specialised unit, had arrived at the school. "I told them, 'Right now, I am on speakerphone with my child. He is on the second floor, clearing rooms one by one from the right side,'" Kwan said.

Without warning, the call with her daughter cut off.

open image in gallery A Buddhist monk leads as workers move a coffin with the body of a victim killed in a deadly shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, at Police General Hospital, in Bangkok, Thailand, August 8, 2026 ( Reuters )

Kwan said ​she started praying, until her daughter called her back after a few minutes. ‌She was unharmed.

Some hours later, the family were reunited at their home in suburban Bangkok, not far from the school. "When we are together, we fight all the time," Khim said of her elder sibling.

"But seeing her this time, I've never loved her this much before."

With the Iran war draining U.S. weapons stockpiles, the Pentagon is reportedly leaning hard on defense companies to bump up production — and fast.

In a memo on Wednesday, Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg gave companies three weeks to lay out how they would “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities.”

“Years-long development cycles are not acceptable,” Feinberg added in the memo, which was obtained by The Washington Post. “We must dramatically accelerate our program schedules and expand our production capacity now.”

The Pentagon confirmed the existence of the August 5 memo and praised Feinberg as a “generational leader” who was “fixing our broken, antiquated, and immensely complex acquisitions system.”

“Working directly with industry leaders to accelerate production is not new,” chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote in a statement to The Independent. “It has been the clear intent of the President and this Secretary from the start.”

open image in gallery The Pentagon is leaning on weapons makers to speed up production as the Iran war reportedly drains key munitions stockpiles ( US Navy )

“The fiscal year 2027 budget currently being considered on Capitol Hill could supercharge this effort today,” he added.

The demands come after weapons manufacturers were reportedly summoned to the White House in July, where they were allegedly urged to lobby Congress to pass another round of funding.

President Donald Trump has insisted the U.S. still has “massive amounts” of weapons, though tempers have reportedly flared over the issue behind the scenes.

The president reportedly confronted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at Camp David last week over the munitions shortage, claiming he thought the problem “had been fixed” already.

open image in gallery The US has expended numerous munitions fighting off swarms of Iranian drones and missile strikes on American bases in the Middle East ( AFP/Getty )

The Trump administration has denied this account, while the president has threatened jail time for the “treasonous” leakers that fueled the reporting.

The U.S. has reportedly used nearly all of its stockpiled long-range precision missiles in the Iran conflict, according to CBS News.

The military has also burned through roughly half of its Patriot interceptors and nearly four-fifths of its Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missile inventory compared to pre-war levels, CNN reported.

The Iran conflict has been something of a strategic mismatch. Tehran, despite possessing a much smaller military than the U.S., has pummeled American bases across the Middle East with low-cost, single-use drones, which the U.S. often has to use expensive interceptors to stop.

The U.S. military had 2,330 Patriot systems and 452 THAAD systems before the war, according to a July report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

As of July 27, the organization estimated 759 to 827 Patriot systems and 234 to 278 THAAD systems remained.

News.title: University opens government-funded lab to help train biomedical scientists
News.content:

A UK university has opened a new government-funded laboratory to help train the next generation of biomedical scientists to work in the NHS and life sciences sector.

The £2.5 million facility at the University of Essex, which includes a dedicated cancer diagnostics laboratory, was funded by the Office for Students.

The investment aims to strengthen training in subjects critical to the UK’s future workforce.

The Bioscience Skills Training and Research Laboratory (BioSTAR-Lab) aims to give students hands-on experience with equipment and techniques used in modern healthcare and life sciences laboratories.

Students studying biomedical science, biotechnology, cancer biology and related degrees will use the laboratories to carry out their research projects.

The facility also includes specialist microbiology and molecular biology laboratories where students will analyse tissue samples, study infectious diseases and use molecular techniques.

open image in gallery The cancer diagnostics laboratory at the University of Essex. (University of Essex/ PA)

Professor Terry McGenity, head of the School of Life Sciences, said: “Here at Essex, we are dedicated to providing a rounded education that is inspired by our world-leading research, which equips our students with the understanding, skills and experience they need to launch their careers in nationally important sectors.

“Hands-on, lab-based research projects provide a transformative experience for our final-year undergraduates and masters students.

“They allow all our students to become part of the research process by carrying out their project alongside experts, where they apply what they’ve learned, and develop critical understanding of a particular area, as well as new technical and analytical skills.

“This new facility will place us at the forefront of training students to be skilled and versatile critical thinkers, who will be ready to work in the NHS and life-sciences sectors.”

The university said the investment comes at a time of growing demand for skilled life scientists, with more than 300,000 people already employed in the sector in the UK.

The lab’s opening comes as the University of Essex launches its first undergraduate biotechnology degree, reflecting growing demand for graduates in a sector that develops vaccines, medicines and diagnostic technologies.

open image in gallery A student examining cancer cells in the lab at the University of Essex. (University of Essex/ PA)

Professor Silke Paulmann, executive dean of the Faculty of Science and Health, said the lab “brings together education, research and real-world application, creating opportunities for students to develop the expertise that will drive future advances in diagnostics, treatments and public health”.

“It will help strengthen the talent pipeline that underpins innovation, economic growth and better health outcomes for communities across the UK,” she said.

The natural gas plant powering a sprawling Amazon data center project in Texas could become the largest climate polluter in the country, despite the company’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2040.

As part of a planned data center campus in Pecos County, the tech giant is investing in an on-site natural gas power plant, the company has confirmed.

The plant is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year, according to documents obtained by The New York Times and the climate research outlet Distilled.

If the final plant matches those specifications, it would be the largest single source of climate pollution in the country, according to the Times, more than doubling the emissions from Alabama’s James H. Miller Jr. Power Plant, a coal facility which emits about 16 million tons of carbon dioxide annually. (Power plants don’t always emit the maximum they are allowed to, and the Amazon facility is still in early-stage construction.)

The company has emphasized that the power plant would not raise rates for Texas residents.

open image in gallery A future Amazon data center will be powered by a gas plant that could become the largest carbon polluter in the country, complicating the company’s climate commitments ( Getty )

“Amazon believes in paying the full costs of powering our operations,” an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement to The Independent on Saturday. “Our new planned data center campus in Pecos County does just that: it’s powered by new on-site generation that won’t raise electricity costs for Texas families and designed to transition to grid-connected service as interconnection timelines allow.”

Amazon is “exploring opportunities for solar energy and battery storage on site,” according to the company. The Pecos project is expected to create “thousands of new jobs,” Amazon said.

The site is reportedly Amazon’s first major investment in off-grid power for a data center.

This puts them in league with “hyperscalers” including Microsoft, Google and Meta, which have all invested in fossil fuel power sources this year as tech companies race to get enough data centers online to meet the ravenous demand for artificial intelligence.

The data campus is the latest complication in Amazon’s highly touted climate commitments.

The company has long faced criticism for working with fossil fuel firms, and its emissions have largely continued to rise since it unveiled its climate commitment in 2019.

open image in gallery High demand for AI has sparked both a data center boom and a power crunch, prompting tech companies to invest in new fossil fuel power sources ( Reuters )

“We recognize that the path to being a more sustainable company is not a straight line,” Amazon said in its recently released sustainability report about 2025. “Though our emissions increased in 2025, we remain steadfast in our commitment to sustainability.”

Asked about the Texas project, Amazon said it remained committed to its climate pledge and pointed to its past record of backing 40 renewable energy projects in the state.

Data centers have increasingly provoked a political backlash, with criticisms honing in on everything from the centers’ environmental emissions to their water use and impact on electricity rates.

This week, the state of Texas pause new data center projects until state electricity regulators could complete an audit of each proposed facility.

“Simply put, Texans must come first,” Republican Governor Greg Abbott wrote in a statement.

The governor’s office noted that approximately 90 percent of the new power requests on the Texas grid are for data centers — facilities that are seeking 474 gigawatts of electricity, more than five times the state’s peak electricity demand record on the grid covering most of the state.

The Trump administration has pushed to speed up data center construction, including by redeveloping federal land to host the facilities, which consume far more electricity than typical data centers and are forecast to imperil global plans to stop the climate crisis.

High demand for data centers, mixed with delays in building new grid connections and power sources, has sent tech companies in search of alternatives, ranging from building bespoke, on-site natural gas plants to investing in future nuclear reactors.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner. I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Huge wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday as officials declared a state of emergency.

The fire in Bald Range doubled in size overnight on Friday, spreading rapidly to about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across British Columbia, including Summerland, Peachland and other districts west of Okanagan Lake.

The region produces most of British Columbia’s wine and is Canada’s second-largest wine-producing area.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had likened the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

Sports.title: ‘I felt that’ – Fans wince as skydiver CRASHES into advertising boards in painful moment as football teams left stunned
Sports.content:
FANS have been left wincing after a pre-match stunt went terribly wrong in the Netherlands.

What was supposed to be entertainment descended into chaos as a parachuter soared into the advertising boards with some force.



Dutch side Go Ahead Eagles had planned an unorthodox delivery of the match ball for their Eredivisie opener against Willem II.

The plan was for a team of skydivers to glide down and place the ball in the centre spot.



However, while there was a team of parachutists, one stood out as he uncontrollably flew towards the pitch.

He ended up smashing into the goal stanchion and the advertising boards in an embarrassing stunt.



The commentator saw the funny side of the incident as he said: “The first injury of the season is a fact, not of a player, but a parachutist.”

And fans also took to social media to react to the bizarre moment.

One wrote: “I felt that. Damn.”

Another said: “Oof, that didn’t go quite as planned.”

A third posted: “That’s quite a landing.”

While a fourth said: “There is such a big goal and you miss that too.”

Thankfully, the parachutist seemed to be OK.

Despite the groans and chuckles from the crowd, he jumped to both feet before saluting his audience.

However, he may think twice before jumping from a plane again!

Sports.title: Prem icon backs Jaissle to shine at Newcastle despite Guimaraes, Tonali & Gordon transfers and says Woltemade will star
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE will instantly get Newcastle fighting for Europe again despite the exodus of stars from the club.

And marmite striker Nick Woltemade is the ideal man to provide the goals for a top-eight finish.



Odds dropped on Newcastle being relegated this week after captain Bruno Guimaraes joined Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon in heading out the exit door.

Jaissle looks to have a huge job on his hands, especially with all three of the Mags’ outfield signings being 20 or younger, to improve on Eddie Howe’s disappointing 12th place finish last season.



Howe himself no longer had the energy for a rebuild and left last week. But former Toon midfielder Dietmar Hamann is adamant that despite the chaos it is a “very good time” for his German compatriot to take over.

Speaking exclusively to Sun Sport via MrQ Casino ahead of Toon’s 2-1 win vs Valencia on Saturday, he said: “Expectations have probably come down a little bit because they went north very quickly with the Saudis taking over a few years ago, and now there’s a chance to go again.

“Eddie did a very good job in getting them into the Champions League and winning the Carabao Cup but now it’s probably time for somebody else to take over and maybe go that next step.

“Newcastle fans will always have fond memories of Eddie Howe, will always have a place in their hearts for him. But it’s a very good time for a new manager to take over there now.”

Jaissle took charge for the first time in a friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla on Saturday. And after a week’s training camp in La Manga, he has just a fortnight to get his men ready to face Liverpool in a bumper Prem opener.

But even though there are many doubters, Hamann is convinced they will be in the fight for Europe come May.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “I’d say a top eight finish because he’s still got some very good players in Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw at the back. And Joelinton is very capable. So there are still some experienced players there, even though some of them are still pretty young in football terms. They’ve got the capabilities to finish well.

“What Jaissle did in Salzburg is he gave young players a chance. He gave them responsibility and, more often than not, they paid him back with performances.

“This is the way to go. this is the way he wants to play as well, a very high intensity game where you need a pretty young team. It fits pretty well.



“The players they bought have got a manager who trusts them. Jaissle is different because he likes to give them a chance. He showed that in Salzburg. So it’s a very good fit for this particular time at Newcastle.”

Much-maligned club-record signing Woltemade arrived with a bang last summer before the goals dried and he was shifted back into a No10 and midfield role last term. The drop-off in form also cost him his place in Germany’s side for the World Cup.

But Hamann has every confidence things will click for him on Tyneside.

He added: “The way Jaissle likes to play always suits a target man like Woltemade. I was very surprised when he started the season so well and then disappeared for pretty much the rest of it.

“There were reports that he’s not settled in Newcastle, which I can’t really understand because there aren’t many better football cities in England, let alone in Europe.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Woltemade’s a very capable player, technically very gifted and brings others into play. It’s very important to have quick players around him. He had that with Gordon last season.

“That’s why there’s probably one or two more incoming. Hopefully, we then see the Woltemade we saw at the start of last season, not just for a three-month spell, but for the full campaign.”

Sports.title: Phil Foden’s girlfriend flogging Three Lions shirts on Vinted after he was dropped by Tuchel
Sports.content:
SNUBBED England ace Phil Foden’s girlfriend is flogging new Three Lions shirts on Vinted — after her World Cup trip with other Wags did not go ahead.

Rebecca Cooke, 25, offers two shirts on the second-hand website for £70 each — the latest white home and red away strips.



The jerseys were modified by a clothing brand which tightened the waists for women.

Other England Wags who did make it to the US and Mexico for the World Cup wore the same tops — including Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie and Anthony Gordon’s girlfriend Annie Keating.



The tops — both in size 12-14 — are listed as being “new with tags”.

They have been modified by Essex-based company A Vintage Fit.

The shirts cost £89.99 on the official England website and the firm charges £90 each to adapt them into a figure-hugging version.

Mum-of-three Rebecca’s England tops are among more than 100 items for sale on her Vinted page.

Also included are four cinched Man City tops — including last season’s grey and bright green third kit for £70 in “perfect condition”.

Two City shirts are vintage from retro footie kit firm Score Draw.



Rebecca’s account states: “Selling new & used authentic items only. Account ran by management team.”



It was not known if she donates to charity any money raised through Vinted.

She had been expecting to go to this year’s World Cup tournament with £15million-a-year Man City star Phil, 26.

He was devastated at being dropped by manager Thomas Tuchel.

A source said: “Perhaps Rebecca had one foot on the plane when she got the tops.”

We approached Rebecca and Phil for comment.



Under-fire Fifa boss Gianni Infantino was last night facing new pressure after it was alleged he paid off a mistress in his job as a Uefa executive.

He denies the allegations.

Sports.title: Barcelona set to launch new bid for Man City superstar Rodri with Enzo Maresca’s side demanding £60million transfer fee
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY boss Enzo Maresca is braced for a new Barcelona bid for Rodri.

The LaLiga champions are sure the midfielder wants to join them this summer.



An offer of £38.5million for Spain’s World Cup-winning captain was laughed off by Etihad chiefs on Friday.

City believe the 30-year-old former Ballon d’Or winner is worth more than £60m — despite having less than 12 months remaining on his current contract.



But Barca transfer guru Deco is ready to test the resolve of the Prem side again, with confidence high at the Nou Camp that they can get a deal done this month.

Rodri, who has been in the North West for the last seven years, is believed to be keen to return to his homeland.



Despite having minor back surgery a couple of weeks ago, he is due back at his current employers this week.

Maresca’s men finish their Far East tour with a game against the midfielder’s old club Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

They will then fly back to Manchester and, by Wednesday, the new boss expects to have his full squad in training at the City Football Academy.

Whether that will include Rodri remains to be seen, with Barcelona determined to get their man despite their recent financial problems.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Meanwhile, City will be on the look-out for a replacement if Rodri does go.

Even though Nico Gonzalez, who they signed for £50m in January last year, plays in a similar position.

The Etihad giants have already spent £116m on Elliot Anderson and are hoping to complete a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Morocco ace, 18, valued at £85m.

Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi have also arrived this year but question marks remain over Rodri and winger Savinho.

Sports.title: Famous napkin contract and Real Madrid transfer threat – How Lionel Messi’s dad guided son through iconic career
Sports.content:
JORGE MESSI died in Rosario aged 68 on Friday night following a long battles with illness.

A driving force behind son Lionel’s outstanding career, tributes poured in for Jorge.



Barcelona expressed their “deepest condolences”, while Jorge’s beloved Newell’s Old Boys spoke of their “deep sorrow and grief”.

A former steel factory worker, Jorge went on to play a huge role in arguably the greatest football career of all time.



He sent Leo, the youngest of three brothers and older sibling to sister Maria Sol, to play for Newell’s from the age of six.

The future superstar obviously immediately oozed talent, but suffered from a growth hormone deficiency which threatened to kibosh his career before it had even started.



When Newell’s stopped paying for treatment, Jorge knew that he had to do something.

He convinced Barcelona to take a look at his son, and accompanied his 14-year-old boy to Europe as he took part in a two-week trial with the Catalan giants in September 2001.



Then-Barca director Carles Rexach was convinced, Leo’s talent was obvious.

But with the LaLiga giants in financial peril at the time, other club chiefs hesitated over whether the swoop for Messi was worth what was considered such a large expense at the time.

Sweating over his son’s growth hormones treatment, which still needed to be paid for, Jorge began looking at other potential moves.



He had been turned down by Argentine giants River Plate, but Real Madrid and Atletico began to circle.

At a now-legendary meeting at a tennis club in December 2001, the deal to bring Messi to Barca was sealed… via a napkin.

Speaking to ESPN, Rexach recalled: “Jorge thought [Barca] were stalling. I wasn’t there and don’t know exactly how things were, but when I met with Jorge I realised he wasn’t clear on anything.

“I suppose he didn’t trust [Barca] and he seemed desperate, so one night I met with [Josep Maria] Minguella and Horacio [Gaggioli] at the Pompeya tennis club and, speaking with Jorge on the phone, he told me, ‘If this isn’t sorted soon, we’re going. I have to return to Buenos Aires and I don’t see anything happening.’

“That was when, thinking on my feet, I decided everything.”



Rexach wrote on a napkin, in Spanish: “In Barcelona, on Dec. 14, 2000, in the presence of Minguella and Horacio, Carles Rexach, FC Barcelona’s sporting director, hereby agrees, under his responsibility and regardless of any dissenting opinions, to sign the player Lionel Messi provided that we keep to the amounts agreed upon.”

The document, which was legally binding, if unorthodox, was signed by Rexach and other Barca chiefs Minguella and Gaggioli – and went on to be flogged at auction two years ago for a staggering £762,400.

From this point onwards, Jorge was his son’s agent, confidante and father rolled into one.



As Leo’s mother Celia and three siblings returned to Rosario, Jorge stayed with his golden child in Barcelona – even insisting that his boy live with him in a city apartment, rather than boarding with the other kids at La Masia.

Messi told Radio del Plata in 2007: “My dad was always by my side.

“Sometimes I would lock myself in my room to cry when we arrived in Barcelona, or my dad would do the same without me seeing him, or thinking I didn’t see him.

“We pretended we were both OK, but we weren’t. My dad even asked me what I wanted to do when we were feeling down, if I wanted to stay or go back, and I wanted to stay, and he stayed with me.”

While Messi progressed through La Masia, Jorge negotiated his first professional contract in 2004, before Barca were forced to fend off significant interest from Inter Milan two years later.



As Leo’s star rose, so did his earning potential – and without a super-agent in tow, it was down to Jorge to capitalise.

The Argentine has had lucrative deals with the likes of Adidas, Pepsi, Budweiser and Konami, to name just a few, during his brilliant career.

In 2017, Jorge negotiated a four-year, €555 million contract, worth around £480m at the time, making his son the highest-paid athlete EVER.



Leo then went on to spend two forgettable seasons at Paris Saint-Germain, before Jorge assisted in another landmark deal three years ago.

In addition to his basic salary at Inter Miami, Messi takes a cut of Apple TV’s broadcast deal with MLS, which is claimed to be worth around $50m (£37m) to the global icon.

Also in 2023, investment firm Play Time was launched – yet another revenue stream for Brand Messi.

Jorge suffered with a long-term illness prior to his death, and was unable to watch his boy at the World Cup this summer – a factor that is thought to have contributed to Messi’s emotional outburst during his side’s opening victory of the tournament.

Leo’s father leaves behind a huge legacy as the man that brought up the greatest footballer of all time.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Newell’s fitting tribute read: “Jorge was the support and the person who, together with his wife, Celia, strengthened the career of the greatest player of all time with vision, rigour and affection.

“His constant support and behind-the-scenes leadership were fundamental in supporting every step of Lionel’s journey.”

Sports.title: Not that close, hey!’ – Erling Haaland turns into ‘jealous boyfriend’ as actor chats with stunning girlfriend Isabel
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY superstar Erling Haaland jokingly turned into a jealous boyfriend in a clip circling on social media.

Italian actor Michele Morrone was seen chatting to Haaland‘s girlfriend Isabel Johansen.



As his partner and Morrone chatted, Haaland said to the camera: “Hey, hey, hey.

“Not that close, not that close.”



However his huge grin immediately afterwards indicated that the big Norwegian was just messing around.

The viral clip came from a video on Haaland’s YouTube channel, where his girlfriend Isabel features regularly.



The Norse raider posted vlog content during the World Cup in the USA, as Norway reached the quarter-finals for the first ever time.

Martin Odegaard, Haaland and Co were eventually stopped by England thanks to a Jude Bellingham double.

The players and fans started the iconic Norway ‘row’ at the World Cup, emulating the behaviour of their Viking ancestors.

Prior to the tournament the team found themselves in hot water with some members of the Norwegian public, as their Viking-style photoshoot was slammed by factions of the country’s media.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

However, the Norway faithful embraced the Viking way as they rowed and rowed all the way to the quarters.

Haaland has evidently continued with his YouTube side-hustle ahead of the beginning of the new Premier League season.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle in fiery debut brawl vs Valencia as Anthony Elanga stretchered off after horror tackle
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE kicked off his Newcastle reign with a brawl against ten-man Valencia.

The German, 38, was fuming as opposition skipper Jose Luis Gaya produced a horror tackle on Anthony Elanga just yards away.



Toon’s new boss instantly raced towards the linesman demanding red – which duly arrived – as players from both sides got into a mini-brawl.

Swedish winger Elanga, Newcastle’s most impressive performer, was eventually stretchered off to cap off an already nightmare start.



Less than four minutes were on the clock when Filip Ugrinic was given all the time in the world to curl home from 25 yards.

Both sides were forced into a reshuffle following Gaya’s red card.



Following the lengthy delay, Jacob Murphy replaced Elanga.

SunSport understands that Elanga suffered a shin contusion, but that it is not as bad as first feared.

He was up and walking not long after the scare, with Newcastle going on to win 2-1.

The Swede would have been looking to impress his new boss Jaissle, having struggled to produce his best form under Howe last term.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Elanga scored three goals and laid on one assist in 49 appearances in his debut Toon campaign.

The year before at Nottingham Forest he had managed six goals and 12 assists.

Newcastle have three friendlies remaining; against Everton, Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg.

They will then begin their Prem campaign by hosting Liverpool on August 23.



And the following week will see them quickly reunite with former star Sandro Tonali, as they travel to North London to face Tottenham.

As for the game against Valencia, Yoanne Wissa was at the double as he and new signing Bazouma Toure stole the show to seal a 2-1 victory in Jaissle’s first game.

This week at Toon’s pre-season La Manga camp, club officials boasted about sprint records being broken in training under the German coach with “intensity” a particular buzzword.

But less than four minutes were on the clock when Filip Ugrinic was given all the time in the world to curl home from 25 yards.

A good strike but Newcastle will need more from new No1 Lukas Hornicek, who joined on Monday in a £25.7m move, once the real stuff gets underway.



Miscommunication with Sven Botman almost led to the defender heading over the onrushing ‘keeper for a second too, only for the ball to bounce a yard wide and out for a corner.

Newcastle wanted a penalty when Will Osula was sent tumbling by Gaya and Elanga had a goal ruled out for offside before his night was cut short.

But it was that moment that changed the game. Fuelled by anger over the tackle and with a man advantage, we began to see glimpses of the “high-energy football” fans had been promised.

Wissa, desperate to impress after a shocking first season at the club, got the goal seven minutes after coming on at the break.



Fellow sub Toure, the £42.5m replacement from Hoffenheim for Gordon down the left wing, forced a defender into panickingly trying to pass back to his goalkeeper. Wissa was on the loose ball in a flash, charging through and slipping it past Stole Dimitrievski’s legs.

The livewire winger provided another scare and needed treatment for a shoulder issue after a tumble before racing through to tee-up Wissa for a tap-in.

There are still plenty of issues for Jaissle, one being the Nick Woltemade conundrum. The head coach showed more energy racing around in front of his dugout and barking out orders than his gangly German striker did in his No10 role. It was his slackness that allowed Ugrinic to pull the trigger for the opener.

But at least Toure’s display provided some chink of light following what has been a bruising summer for the Toon Army.

Speaking after, Jaissle said: “We will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot, we’re quite balanced. We know what it is about. Now it’s pre-season and we still have a lot to work on.



“First of all, I’m really happy that there are no serious injuries. Anthony, we are happy and it seems to be not serious. That’s the most important thing and, of course, winning games helps always to gain confidence.

“But we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well in the camp. There was a clear commitment to see in each session. We had a hard load, so therefore now they deserve two days off, and then we start again.”

Asked whether his young summer signings are ready to face Liverpool in the Premier League opener in a fortnight, he added: “That’s already too long ahead to think about now if you ask me about the starting eleven for Liverpool.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m just here now a couple of days. We have still three more friendly matches where we will see many things and that’s our goal, just to give everyone the chance to show up.

“And if you ask me about the three signings, I was not involved, that was before my time, as you know, so, but I’m happy that they’re here.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford pictured partying with bikini-clad women on luxury boat as he shares £270 a bottle champagne & sips beer
Sports.content:
FOOTBALLER Marcus Rashford becomes Flash Rash on holiday as he throws his cash around for a group of girls on a luxury boat.

The England and Man Utd star shared a £270 bottle of Armand de Brignac Brut Gold champagne with pals.



He also wore an expensive pair of Louis Vuitton trainers, a chunky silver chain with a pendant that reads “Home is where the heart is” and a £23,000 black Hublot Square Bang Unico watch.

The 28-year-old, said to be paid £325,000 a week, enjoyed his post-World Cup break on a hired boat on the French Riviera with ten female pals — but with no sign of his girlfriend, Lucia Loi.



A witness said: “The England lads played so well at the World Cup and deserve some downtime after a heroic third-place finish.

“It was kind of Marcus to share his time off with a group of stunning women on the ocean waves. He’s really living the dream.”



After a year-long loan to Spanish La Liga side Barcelona, Rashford is set for a return to boyhood club United for the new Premier League season, starting later this month.

He is due to re-join Michael Carrick’s outfit next week, but has also been linked with an £80million transfer to clubs including Arsenal and Spurs.

Rashford made his debut for United aged 18 in 2016 and went on to make 426 appearances in all competitions.

But he has not pulled on a United shirt since the Europa League tie against Czech side Viktoria Plzen in December 2024 and fell out with former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

When Amorim left him out of the team for an 11th successive game, the manager said he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital than Rashford.



Amorim was in a stand-off with the England international, who previously declared he wanted a “new challenge” away from the club he had spent more than a decade representing.



United sacked Amorim on January 5, 2026, after 14 months in charge, following a 1–1 draw against Leeds United and growing tensions with the club hierarchy.

Rashford could make his return in a pre-season friendly against Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday.

Then on Saturday, United play AC Milan — where Amorim is now the manager.

Sports.title: Wissa double gives Newcastle boss Jaissle winning start at 10-man Valencia
Sports.content:
Substitute Yoane Wissa scored twice to give Matthias Jaissle a winning start as Newcastle boss with a 2-1 comeback pre-season win at 10-man Valencia.

But the friendly at the Mestalla threatened to be overshadowed by Jose Gaya's red-card horror tackle on Anthony Elanga, which saw the Newcastle winger stretchered off in the first half and led to both sets of players clashing.

Fortunately for the Sweden international, his injury does not appear to be serious, with Elanga later up and walking after a contusion to the shin.



Image: Tempers flared after Jose Gaya's challenge saw Anthony Elanga stretchered off

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Jaissle was "relaxed" over Elanga's injury.

The German said: "It seems to be not bad, so we are pleased. I hope it's true, then he can start again next week."

He added: "Of course I was in fear [it was a serious injury], definitely, but now I'm more relaxed as the medical department is showing almost green lights, and there's nothing serious."

Who played for Newcastle? Hornicek; Shahar (M Miley 46), Thiaw (Johnson 72), Botman, Pivas (Charlton 67); Bamba (Steur 46), Ramsey (Joelinton 67); Elanga (J Murphy 39), Woltemade (Willock 67), Barnes (Toure 46); Osula (Wissa 46).

Unused subs: Gillespie, Harris, Finneran, Neave.

Elanga's injury after Valencia's Filip Ugrinic's stunning fifth-minute opener had given Jaissle a nightmare start to life in the Newcastle dugout.

But his half-time changes sparked a Toon turnaround with new signings Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur impressing.

It was last summer's signing Wissa who pounced on a mistake to level in the 52nd minute.

New arrival Toure then broke clear of the Valencia defence to unselfishly set up Wissa for a tap-in to complete the comeback in the 76th minute.

Toure should have had a second assist after fine work down the left, but Jacob Murphy put over his cross in stoppage time.

The win brings some relief to Newcastle on the day they lost their captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

Jaissle's next pre-season test will come on Wednesday as his new side face Everton at Murrayfield in Edinburgh.

Image: Newcastle's Nick Woltemade (left) started at the Mestalla

Wissa's fresh start under Jaissle

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie at the Mestalla:

"A good end to a positive week in Spain for Newcastle - and a trophy for Jaissle in his first match in charge as they lift the 'Orange Cup'.

"Some impressive signs from new signings Aladji Bamba, Steur and Toure.

"Newcastle's travelling fans sent home from The Mestalla with a spring in their step.

"One major positive was Wissa's performance.

"Newcastle really need him to come good this season. It was a huge £55m outlay on a 29-year-old, and last season was a nightmare for him.

"He looks sharp and is coming off a good World Cup showing. Maybe this could be a fresh start for the striker."

Jaissle keeping 'balanced' after debut win

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle speaking at his post-match press conference:

"First of all, I'm really happy that there are no serious injuries. Anthony, we are happy, and it seems to be okay, actually - that was the most important thing.

"Of course, winning games always helps to gain confidence, but we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well in the camp; there was a pure commitment in each session.

"We had a hard load, so therefore now we deserve two days off, and then we start again.

"It was a friendly today; we will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot.

"We're quite balanced; we know what it is about. Now it's pre-season, and we're still looking to work on it.

"It's just a journey; we don't want to hang onto that.

"The victory is higher than it is, but also we don't see the losses lower than it is then, so we should be quite balanced in our approach.

"We should just analyse the situation and develop from there, and that's what we're going to do.

"Now next week, there are things we need to work on, definitely."

Sports.title: McKenna becomes middleweight world champ with dream homecoming win
Sports.content:
Ireland's Aaron McKenna defeated Etinosa Oliha to become a middleweight world champion.

For McKenna this fight in Dublin was a dream homecoming. The Irish middleweight had pursued his career across America, sparring in some of the world's best gyms and amassing an undefeated pro record.

This contest, for the vacant IBF middleweight title, was his first world title fight and his first professional contest in Ireland.

With brother Stevie taking a spectacular knockout earlier, McKenna made a memorable entrance, wildly cheered into the ring by the 3Arena crowd, so loudly that the floor was almost rumbling.

But he didn't let emotions carry him away at the start of the fight. He edged forward onto the front foot, feinting. He timed a left hook as Oliha, unbeaten himself coming in, stepped to him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna had an incredible entrance ahead of his IBF world middleweight title fight with Etinosa Oliha, first coming into Sinead O'Connor's The Foggy Dew and then Faithless' Insomnia!

McKenna let his jab flicker out. His hands were quick, his right streaked in and McKenna used his left hook to let a cross blast through.

But the Italian wrested the second round his way, thumping through right hooks, punches McKenna felt, to show that he too could launch meaningful attacks.

McKenna ground forward, stifling his own long-range work but bodily forcing Oliha back.

When he did strike his opponent with a reaching right, the crowd roared and as the fight progressed into its second half McKenna did move more on his toes, darting back to scrape his left hook into the side of Oliha's head.

The Italian looked to rip hooks into him but McKenna marshalled him to the ropes and slugged Oliha with a left hook.

Image: McKenna and Oliha were both unbeaten coming into this world title fight

McKenna imposed himself again in the ninth round but Oliha, a solid operator, showed little sign of wilting.

In the 10th round McKenna circled out and reeled off double jabs. As they grappled in a clinch though, Oliha unleashed a flurry that caught the Irishman.

McKenna briefly put space between them with a cross to the chin. He scored to the body with thudding right hooks too.

Oliha charged from his corner with a long one-two to start the 11th round. With flashier work, McKenna landed a left uppercut off his jab. Oliha though hacked back at him with a right hook up close.

McKenna continued to punch in greater volume. A clash saw him cut on the forehead just before the end of the 11th. He trusted in a hefty right hook as a response.

Image: McKenna tears into Oliha.

He didn't want or need to take risks in the last round. He moved sharply, striking an increasingly desperate Oliha with jabs and the crowd all around him stood up cheering, clapping and chanting his name.

McKenna worked an uppercut, Oliha drove in a right but even when McKenna took shots he didn't let them shake him as he closed out a unanimous decision.

When that final bell chimed, McKenna rushed to the corner post and jumped up onto the ropes to celebrate.

As soon as the words "from Monaghan" were declared by the ring announcer, confirming McKenna a 118-110, 117-111 and 116-112 victor, the arena burst into deafening cheers once again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna was in buoyant mood after beating Etinosa Oliha to become IBF world middleweight champion in front of his home crowd in Dublin.

"A new world champion. I've been saying it for years. A big thank you to Zuffa Boxing for giving me this platform and bringing a fight back to Ireland for me," McKenna beamed afterwards.

"I've been a professional for nine years and never got the chance to fight in Ireland. Why? Just look at these beautiful fans.

"I never lost discipline in training. There were times when I wondered whether I'd ever get the chance.

"My dad [their trainer] sacrificed his whole life for me and my brother, dedicating everything to helping us chase our dreams.

"Finally, I've got my hands on this."

Sports.title: 'Good signs' for Man Utd as Mbeumo scores in encouraging  draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo earned Man Utd a 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg, a pre-season friendly which left boss Michael Carrick encouraged by the "good signs" from his side.

A slow start, which saw Liverpool-linked Ibrahim Mbaye tuck in a PSG opener after just two minutes and the European champions - despite missing many of their star names - stretch United, was overcome and fears of an injury to Mason Mount were also allayed, with the midfielder later seen walking freely after being forced off during the first half.

The standout Amad Diallo was key to United shifting the momentum. He won the ball back high up the pitch to tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish for United's equaliser and proved too hot to handle for the PSG defence into the half-time break.

Mbeumo would have added to his tally had PSG's Matvey Safonov not been in such sharp form, although the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering Joshua Zirkzee way outside of his area.

Image: Youri Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

At the other end, United goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a hamstring issue and had to be replaced. It was a problem which appears more significant than the injury Mount seemingly got to his left foot, which Carrick later suggested was just a kick. With Altay Bayindir loaned to Celta Vigo and Radek Vitek sold to Middlesbrough, 23-year-old Dermot Mee came on for his debut.

There were late chances for Tyler Fletcher, Shea Lacey and captain Bruno Fernandes - who linked up excitingly with new signing Youri Tielemans. United weren't able to find a winner but this was a performance to be positive about.

Man Utd team news: Tielemans on for debut as Bruno returns Youri Tielemans came on as a second-half sub to make his Man Utd debut in Sweden. Captain Bruno Fernandes also entered the action for his first minutes of pre-season.



Michael Carrick had made just one change from the side which started the win over Atletico Madrid last weekend, with Noussair Mazraoui coming in for Leny Yoro.



PSG were without their France stars Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue or Bradley Barcola.

The key moments from Gothenberg...

2: GOAL! Ibrahim Mbaye tucks in the opener at the back post from Dro Fernandez's cross after Ayden Heaven is unable to cut it out.

4: SHOT! PSG threaten again with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia denied from distance by Tom Heaton.

16: BLOCK! Andrey Santos slides in to block Mbaye's shot over the bar with United stretched.

20: INJURY! Mason Mount is forced off injured with an apparent foot injury.

32: GOAL! Amad Diallo wins the ball back high up the pitch and feeds Bryan Mbeumo who cracks an equaliser across goal and into the bottom corner.

Man Utd on the front foot Man Utd had 24 touches in the opposition box. PSG managed just seven.

36: NO PENALTY! Amad's appeals are waved away when Willian Pacho nudges him as he goes for a header.

38: SAVE! For the second time in the match Mbeumo tests PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov with a free-kick shot.

48: INJURY! Heaton injures his right hamstring making a clearance and Dermot Mee comes on in his place.

54: SAVE! Stunning stop from Safonov to deny Mbeumo's shot towards the top corner from outside the box.

72: DRAMA! Safonov rushes out of his box and clatters Zirkzee with his shoulder as United try to counter no foul is given and after Jack Fletcher declines a long-range shot at the unguarded goal, Shea Lacey's effort is blocked behind.

87: CHANCES! Dalot's cross is met by Tyler Fletcher but he twice has efforts blocked before Lacey lashes over from a tight angle

89: CLOSE! Fernandes whips a shot just wide of the far post with a bouncing shot from outside the box.

Carrick 'enjoyed' PSG draw: 'We should have scored more goals'

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick to MUTV:

"I enjoyed it. Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should've scored more goals.

"Very different to what we've played against, the boys adapted really well, so there were a lot of positives from the game. The things we were trying to get out of the game, a lot of it was there.

"It's good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don't always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there."

Attacking positives for Man Utd in PSG draw

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"Man Utd's attack caught the eye on Saturday, with Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo looking sharp and the connection between Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes already clicking.

"Amad played a big part in shifting the momentum United's way after PSG's fast start. In the final third he won the ball back and passed it more than any other player on the pitch.

"That impact with and without the ball was clear when he found Mbeumo for the equaliser - and the striker's finish was excellent.

"Mbeumo could easily have scored more but for some good goalkeeping, landing four shots on target. No other player managed more than one.

"Debutant Tielemans and returning captain Fernandes could not be expected to be so sharp making their first minutes of pre-season - but still they produced some nice link-up play and signs they will be a big influence in this coming campaign.

"Tielemans' passing from deep was classy; Fernandes was immediately a threat around the edge of the box.

"As Michael Carrick said afterwards, 'good signs' for the season ahead."
