World.title: Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood
World.content:
Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood

By Zoila Palma: The Belize @45 Workshop, a three-day professional development training, was held from August 5 to 7, 2026, bringing together educators from across the country to examine what Belize’s independence really means.

The training was a collaborative effort of the Institute for Social and Cultural Research (ISCR), the Belize Archives and Records Service (BARS), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science & Technology (MOECST), specifically Ms. Ruby Reyes of the Belizean Studies Curriculum and Assessment Unit, the George Price Centre for Peace and Development, the University of Belize, and Galen University.

During the training, historian and diplomat Assad Shoman challenged educators to reflect on the “role of teachers and students in shaping Belize’s future.”

The event included virtual sessions and an in-person learning session at the George Price Centre for Peace and Development in Belmopan, equipping educators with new tools and perspectives to bring Belize’s history and independence journey to life for students.

Organizers emphasized that Belize’s independence is not simply an achievement of the past, but an ongoing process, underscoring the message: “Independence is the beginning!

World.title: Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub

By Zoila Palma: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and several other parts of the United States travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services brought directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The three-day Evanston Diaspora Hub runs from August 7 to 9. The event provides passport and nationality services, including first-time and renewal passport applications, as well as applications for Belizean nationality by descent.

The ministry says that the outreach provides a more convenient way to complete important documentation without having to travel to Belize. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission, making mobile outreach efforts particularly valuable for Belizeans living far from those locations.

The Evanston hub also highlighted the strong community ties among Belizeans living in the United States. Some Chicago-area residents noted that they have built a vibrant Belizean community and are preparing to host a fundraiser on Saturday to provide scholarships to 14 Belizean-American students attending school.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, visited the hub alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy, as officials engaged with Belizeans accessing the services.

The Evanston initiative follows other diaspora outreach efforts by the Government of Belize in the United States. Earlier this year, approximately 230 passports and 17 nationality certificates were delivered to Belizeans abroad during another outreach initiative, reflecting continued demand for documentation services within Belizean communities across the United States.

World.title: Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub

By Hugh O’Brien: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and the larger United States, including Texas, Washington and Colorado, travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services being offerred directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The Diaspora Mobile Hub, being held from August 7 to 9, is providing Belizeans living in the United States with an opportunity to complete nationality and passport applications without having to travel to Belize or wait for an appointment at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.

While many of those attending came from Evanston, Chicago and surrounding communities, others travelled hundreds or even thousands of miles to take advantage of the outreach initiative. Several Belizeans from the Dallas area made the journey to Evanston to submit applications and complete other documentation processes.

In a public statement posted on its Facebook page, the Ministry said “Some visitors came to renew their Belizean passports, while others submitted first-time passport applications. Families also visited the hub to apply for Belizean nationality by descent, allowing eligible children and other descendants born outside Belize to formally establish their Belizean nationality.”

The Ministry said that these services are being provided through the Nationality and Passports Department as part of the Ministry’s broader effort to bring essential government services closer to Belizeans living abroad.

“For members of the diaspora, having services available in a U.S. city can significantly reduce the time, cost and logistical challenges associated with completing important documentation. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.”

For this reason, according to the Ministry, Evanston became a destination this weekend not only for Belizeans living in Illinois, but also for members of the diaspora who travelled from across the United States.

“For some families, the visit was simply about renewing a passport and maintaining the ability to travel using Belizean documentation. For others, particularly parents seeking nationality by descent for their children, the process represented another way of passing their connection to Belize from one generation to the next,” said the Ministry.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, attended the Ministry’s immigration outreach alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy.

Belizean nationality by descent is available to qualifying persons born outside Belize based on Belizean parentage.

The Evanston Diaspora Mobile Hub continues will conclude on Sunday, August 9.

World.title: Jamaica’s Edwards snatches triple jump gold at World U20 Champs
World.content:
In this March 2026 file photo, Jamaica College star Michael-Andre Edwards displays his gold medal after winning the Class 1 Boys’ triple jump final, with a leap of 16.25m., to close out his Champs career. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

OREGON, USA – Michael Andre Edwards thought he would be able to jump “about 16.80m” but surprised himself with a dramatic final round 17.08m (1.1m/s) leap to snatch the gold medal at the World Athletics Under- 20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Edwards, who started slowly, trailed his good friend American Miles Nesmith going into the final round, when he produced the jump of his life on the biggest stage.

After his dramatic win, he said he never expected he would be jumping this far this soon but never thought 17.00m was out of his reach.

He twice bettered his previous personal best of 16.30m set in July, with 16.71m in the fifth round and then his big jump a round later. He joins national under-20 record holder Jaydon Hibbert,17.87m, and James Beckford, 17.29m, as the only Jamaican juniors to jump over 17.00m in the triple jump.

Edwards is also the second Jamaican man to win the triple jump after Hibbert won it in 2022.

This was Jamaica’s first gold of the champions and third medal after Gary Card and Shanoya Douglas won silver medals in their respective 100m finals on Thursday.

Nesmith, who was second to Edwards at the Penn Relays in April, took the silver medal with a personal best 16.79m (1.0m/s) and China’s Zhuoyue Wang was third with 16.36m (0.9m/s).

Edwards, who needed just one jump, 16.00m, to qualify from the prelims, started slowly with a 13.76m (1.4m/s) but qualified for the final with a 16.23m (-0.3m/s) in the third round before he got into second place with 16.71 (0.5m/s) in the fifth round.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Hurting Jamaica
World.content:
An inflatable obstacle course at the entry fee-free Harmony Beach Park in Montego Bay, St James.

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett has criticised people who he says are creating a false impression internationally that Jamaicans are being denied access to the country’s beaches.

Speaking at the 2026 Artisan Village Food Festival in Falmouth on Thursday, Bartlett argued that the facts do not support the narrative being circulated overseas and the false claims are damaging Jamaica’s reputation and costing the Government money to correct.

“We have 70 [public bathing beaches] in Jamaica, all around the island. And of that 70 only 10 of them are paid beaches. And then only five of that you would pay a decent money to go to,” Bartlett said.

“And yet, some of us, when you hear what we say to the international media… you would believe that every beach in Jamaica is just locked off, and that’s not fair to Jamaica. That’s not fair to us,” added Bartlett.

He argued that concerns may arise about access to specific beaches, but insisted that isolated issues should not be used to broad-brush the country.

“So we say, if you have an issue with one, or two, all right, let’s talk about that. Let’s deal with it because everywhere in the world you go, there’s an issue. But we must deal with it and resolve it, and not define ourselves by it,” argued Bartlett.

The tourism minister said the Government has had to invest in advertising and promotional campaigns to counter misinformation in the international media.

“You know as minister of tourism how much trouble I get on international press to go and explain to them that it is not true? Then we have to spend money with advertising agents… to tell them seh nothing nuh go so,” Bartlett said.

He urged Jamaicans to resolve national challenges internally rather than tarnishing the country’s image overseas.

“So we have to help ourselves. Where we have a problem, let us resolve it. Let us see where the difficulties are, talk about it, deal with it at home, solve it at home. And, as Miss Lou seh, ‘Don’t wash your dirty linen abroad,’ because when you believe you are hurting your neighbour, you’re not hurting your neighbour, you’re hurting your country and, in the end, yourself,” Bartlett added.

He lamented what he described as a tendency among some Jamaicans to highlight only the country’s shortcomings.

“Some of us enjoy beating up little Jamaica. Some of us enjoy saying all the negative things about the country, and some people I hear say things like Jamaica refuse to make its people enjoy the beaches. I never hear anything like that,” he said.

Bartlett urged Jamaicans to use the country’s 64th anniversary of Independence to embrace a new conversation and project a more positive image of the nation.

“And as we do that, the second thing I want to concern my mind and to get you into my thoughts on is how it is that we project ourselves as a people and as a country,” Bartlett said.

“The world views us through our own eyes and through our prisms. The world sees us the way we see ourselves, but most importantly, the way we express who we are to the world,” he added.

Bartlett said Jamaica’s 64th Independence anniversary should mark the beginning of a more positive national outlook.

“So, on this 64th birthday, let us resolve to have a new conversation, a new narrative, a positive contribution to ourselves, as together we grow. As we recover from Melissa, we recover stronger and better, and we build this great little piece of rock. In the words of Miss Lou, ‘We little but we tallawah,’” he said.

Official data show Jamaica possesses approximately 1,022 kilometres of coastline, of which approximately 29 per cent (300 kilometres) consists of sandy beaches.

World.title: Potential investors wary as tourism GCT increase looms
World.content:
HERON... I have had calls from a number of investors who have told me point blank that they are concerned

MONTEGO BAY, St James — The Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association (JHTA) says the uncertainty surrounding the Government’s proposed increase in the general consumption tax (GCT) on the sector is causing concern among potential investors.

According to JHTA President O’Brian Heron, the proposal has left some investors uneasy as they assess their plans for the local tourism industry.

“I have had calls from a number of investors who have told me point blank that they are concerned and they really want us to get this GCT issue resolved as quickly as possible because it does affect their ability, it does affect their excitement and their passion and their trust in the ability to invest in destination Jamaica,” Heron told the Jamaica Observer.

His comments come as tourism stakeholders and Government representatives continue discussions aimed at finding common ground on the proposal to increase the GCT applicable to sections of the sector from 10 per cent to 15 per cent.

“There are concerns; a number of investors are restive at this time and are really waiting to see what the outcome will be of these GCT discussions and negotiations with the Government,” Heron added on the margins of a HEART/NSTA Trust Priority Sector Industry Roundtable with tourism stakeholders on Friday.

The proposed increase was announced as part of the Government’s revenue measures during the 2026-27 Budget Debate, prompting widespread concern across the tourism industry.

According to Heron, the additional tax burden would further compound the challenges the sector is facing as it works to remain viable.

“What we are particularly concerned about is, our industry has been subject to a number of shocks over the years. From COVID-19, on the heels of that we had Hurricane Beryl, then there is Hurricane Melissa, there is increasing oil prices and fuel prices all over, there is significant pressure being borne by the industry right now that is trying to recover… trying to settle insurance claims and this is going to squeeze the industry to a point where we risk our own competitiveness,” added Heron.

He said these concerns prompted the JHTA to approach the Ministry of Finance for discussions on the plan.

“I believe that our focus and our push with ensuring the Government understands the affordability issue and the profitability issue is something we need to remain very strident on, we need to remain very steadfast on,” the JHTA president said.

He told the Observer that some progress was made during a recent meeting with officials of the Ministry of Finance.

“Where we are when we left the conversation with the minister of finance [Fayval Williams] is that we agreed to form a working group to really explore alternative solutions around opportunities to help the Government to meet its fiscal objectives without squeezing the industry to a point of not really being able to be competitive, or to perform,” Heron said.

The JHTA president argued that the tourism industry has consistently made significant contributions to Government revenue and continues to do so.

“The industry is not anti-tax. As a matter of fact, we already pay our fair share of taxes, whether it is through corporate taxes or other statutory taxes that actually exist,” he explained.

“To operate a hotel, we’re also subjected to a number of licences and fees that are renewable every year and come with their own sets of inspections,” Heron said.

World.title: Grand Gala honours Rock resilience
World.content:
Prime Minister Andrew Holness acknowledges the roar of the crowd. Garfield Robinson

As the island’s annual Emancipendence celebrations culminated in grand style on Thursday evening, thousands of Jamaicans draped in black, green and gold descended on the National Stadium with one purpose: To celebrate the nation’s 64th anniversary of nationhood and pay tribute to the unbreakable spirit that has carried the country through triumph and tragedy.

Coming less than a year after the devastation of Hurricane Melissa, one of the most destructive storms in the nation’s history, this year’s Grand Gala carried a deeper significance. Beneath the pageantry, the music, and the fireworks was a quiet but resolute declaration from the Jamaican people: We are still standing.

Throughout the evening, the resilience of a nation took centre stage as generations of entertainers, cultural practitioners, and musicians came together in a dazzling display of Jamaican excellence.

Among the night’s most anticipated moments were the performances from honorees Busy Signal and Wayne Wonder, both of whom reminded patrons why their music continues to occupy a treasured place in the country’s cultural landscape.

Busy Signal delivered an electrifying set, moving effortlessly through crowd favourites such as

Step Out Inna Mi Black, Bumaye, and

Nah Go Jail Again. Yet, it was his stirring performance of

Jamaica Love that became the emotional heartbeat of the night.

As the stadium lights dimmed, the entertainer urged patrons to illuminate the venue with their phone flash lights. In an instant, thousands of tiny lights pierced the darkness, transforming the stadium into what seemed a sea of stars. What followed was less of a performance and more of a collective expression of national pride as the crowd joined in a choir-like rendition of the song that many have come to regard as Jamaica’s unofficial second anthem.

Earlier in the evening, fellow honoree Wayne Wonder delivered a short but memorable set that traced the soundtrack of his decades-long career. Hits including No Letting Go, Saddest Day, I Don’t Know Why, Joyride, and Informer reverberated throughout the stadium, proving exactly why he too was deserving of the night’s Reggae Icon Award.

With each song Wayne Wonder showcased a musical legacy that has transcended generations, one that continues to bridge the gap between Jamaica’s past and present.

The evening’s nostalgia extended far beyond the honorees. A spirited Festival song sound clash featuring DJ Oliver and DJ Rasarella sent patrons on a journey through time as classics such as B am Bam, Baba Boom, Sweet and Dandy, Chiquitita, and Land of My Birth filled the space.

The celebration of Jamaica’s musical heritage continued when Roy Rayon took to the stage with his 1987 Festival Song winner, Thanks and Praises. The familiar melody had patrons clapping and singing along, signalling that the festivities for year 64 were in fully swing.

Then came the gospel segment, a fitting reminder that faith remains woven into the fabric of Jamaican identity.

Kevin Downswell captivated the audience with spirited renditions of You Make Me Stronger, Carry Me, and If It’s Not You, delivering a performance that balanced reverence with infectious energy.

Sebastian Braham followed with his beloved Hard Road to Travel medley, breathing new life into timeless favourites, including I Am Determined, Some Sweet Day, I Know Where I’m Going, and I Am Under the Rock.

Sister Pat transformed the stadium into a revival ground, leading patrons through classics such as Massa God A God, The Lord Is My Shepherd, and Come By Here, Lord. As thousands danced and sang along, her call for Jamaicans to give thanks for 64 years of nationhood was met with thunderous applause.

The programme also paid homage to Jamaica’s cultural roots with a breathtaking dance presentation,

Ode to Africa, and a musical showcase titled Celebrating Kingston: The Creative City of Music, which highlighted the genres born on Jamaican soil — mento, ska, rocksteady, reggae, and dancehall. This segment saw performances from dBURNZ, Janeen Mills, Noel Ellis, and reggae icon Marcia Griffiths.

Yet perhaps the night’s most moving moment came during the annual drone show. Already a crowd favourite, this year’s spectacle carried an emotional weight that transcended entertainment. Against the darkness of the night sky, 1,000 drones recreated not only the symbols synonymous with Jamaican culture, but also the destructive path carved by Hurricane Melissa in October 2025.

What unfolded was not simply a retelling of devastation but a testament to survival. As stories of communities rebuilding and neighbours supporting neighbours accompanied the display, the narrative shifted from loss to resilience. Praying hands illuminated the night sky as Chris Malachi’s Brighter Day echoed throughout the stadium. In that moment, Jamaica’s greatest strength became unmistakably clear — its people, their faith and unwavering determination to rise. Vibrant firework displays brought the curtains down on another Grand Gala celebration in recognition of 64 years of Independence and resilience of the Jamaican spirit.

World.title: US court orders halt to Trump ballroom construction
World.content:
A view of the ongoing construction of a helipad (left) and ballroom (right) at the White House, as seen from the Washington Monument observation deck in Washington, DC on July 23, 2026.Photo: AFP

WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — An appeals court on Friday upheld an order halting work on Donald Trump’s prized White House ballroom, setting up another battle in the Supreme Court over the limits of presidential authority.

The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit, which had allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, agreed with a lower court that such a massive White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress.

It stayed its own decision for two weeks to give Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene.

The Republican president lashed out after the 2-1 ruling, calling it “horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful”.

The two judges in the majority were appointed by Democratic presidents, while the dissenter was nominated by Trump himself.

The president vowed in a lengthy social media post to immediately appeal to the Supreme Court, while reiterating his argument that the entire project represented a matter of national security.

Trump initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas, but has since repeatedly pointed to the concurrent addition of an underground military bunker and other security features.

Under the district judge’s initial order, work was to be allowed to continue only on a limited set of structures, including those that were underground.

“This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom,” the majority wrote Friday.

“What it does mean is that the defendants may not do so during the district court’s expeditious litigation without securing congress’s authorisation, as the Constitution and laws require.”

Trump, who has repeatedly complained that the White House lacks sufficient space for grand galas such as state dinners, unilaterally ordered construction of the massive ballroom.

Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the White House’s entire historic East Wing.

Since then, photos have shown significant work on a basement complex, with some concrete walls rising up above ground.

Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but media reports in June showed that significant taxpayer funds were going to the project, which could cost as much as US$600 million.

While the White House initially cited a US$200-million price tag for the project, it quickly doubled the estimate to US$400 million.

The ballroom is just one of Trump’s pet projects to leave his mark on Washington by the time he leaves office in 2029, along with a renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other parks, as well as the construction of a gigantic arch.

Several of the projects have similarly faced legal challenges, but the ballroom project would be the first to reach the Supreme Court.

World.title: Three alleged exotic dancers from Dom Rep charged with work permit breaches
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — Three women from the Dominican Republic and two Jamaican nightclub owners appeared in the St James Parish Court on Wednesday facing charges of working without a permit and aiding and abetting that offence.

Marsol Beaz Beaz, Yahaira Jimena Tejeda Sanchez and Naiomi Perez, of the Dominican Republic, appeared alongside Jamaicans Camoy Spence and Nicholas Ricketts before Parish Judge Diahann Bernard.

All five are represented by attorney-at-law Adrian Dayes.

The allegations stem from an operation conducted on August 3 by members of the St James Police Division and the Trafficking in Persons Unit at a nightclub on Barnett Street, Montego Bay, St James, following information about suspected human trafficking activities at the establishment.

According to the prosecution, the cops saw the three Dominican women with several Jamaican exotic dancers at the nightclub.

The women were interviewed and subsequently arrested and charged with working without a permit, while the nightclub owners were charged with aiding and abetting working without a permit.

During the hearing, Dayes told the court that his clients were lawfully in Jamaica and were not working at the time of the operation.

A translator from the Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency assisted with the proceedings but Dayes told the court that the defence was still taking instructions and preferred to use its own translator rather than relying on the State.

The clerk of court clerk indicated that the three women have permission to remain in Jamaica until September 2 and indicated that the prosecution anticipates calling additional witnesses.

The clerk further indicated that the surety who previously secured bail for the three women advised that the arrangement only covered Wednesday’s court appearance.

Bernard subsequently granted the three women bail in the sum of $100,000 each, in their own surety, and ordered them to surrender their travel documents.

The matter was adjourned to September 2 for case management. Bail for Spence and Ricketts was extended.

World.title: More to come
World.content:
Jamaica’s Shanoya Douglas (left) and American Mia Maxwell (centre) both lunge for the finish line in the women’s 100m final at the World Under-20 Championships on Thursday at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon. Maxwell won in 11.14 seconds, just ahead of Douglas, 11.17. At right, Italy’s Kelly Ann Edimo finished third to take the bronze medal in 11.27. Paul Reid

OREGON, USA — Shanoya Douglas says her quest for an individual gold medal at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships is not over, as she gets ready for her preferred 200m after taking the silver in the 100m on Thursday.

Douglas and Gary Card, who came into the championships as world leaders in the 100m, were beaten into second-place finishes by Americans Mia Maxwell and Tate Taylor, respectively. It was only the second time athletes from the same country had won both gold medals in the 100m at the same Under-20 Championships, after Noah Lyles and Candace Hill won in 2016 in Bydgoszcz, Poland.

These were the first medals for Jamaica at the championships.

Both Douglas and Card had advanced to their respective 200m semi-finals after qualifying in the first round on Friday’s morning session.

Douglas, who also leads the women’s 200m ranking, says she was happy with her silver medal — her second individual medal at the World Under-20s — after winning bronze in the 200m two years ago in Lima, Peru. She, however, underlined that she is still hungry for more.

“The championships are not over yet. I still have the 200m, and there is still room to correct and to get my mental space where it is supposed to be — and it is not easy to win all the time,” she said. “I am not going to lay down and take silver; I am coming back stronger and better in the 200m.”

Douglas, who broke the national junior record twice this year, has a best of 22.11 seconds, and tied for third-best all-time with American legend Allyson Felix, says she knows what to fix.

“There are some tweaks and twerks to getting me where I’m at, and it’s on a bigger stage where anything is possible. It is just to come out on the day and perform. I felt like [Mia] came out on the day, and that’s it. She got the edge over me this time [but] it’s not gonna be the last. We’ll see each again on a different stage where we run together, and I feel like I’ll be winning too.”

Card was grateful for his medal. And after placing sixth two years ago in Lima, Peru, he said things could have been different and he was grateful.

“I know I could have done better but, just to be honest, just to be in the moment right here, healthy, being able to do what I did, it could have gone so many other ways, could have gone much worse but I’m just glad that God allowed me to finish healthy and came home with this medal. So, I’m grateful,” Card said.

“It’s very good that I’m one of the best under-20 athletes right now. We’re all going to be seniors soon — and all seniors also came through the junior ranks — and there is not a lot of generations [of athletes] who have performed like how we perform out here so everybody should be grateful. I feel like everybody should be grateful, and everybody should just be happy about it,” added Card.

He had high praises for Taylor, who he said was an “amazing person … So I’m very glad for him, and I was honoured to be sort of seen to be his rival in this event. I am grateful, I know he’s grateful, so I’m just glad it both worked out well, in some way, for both of us.”

Card got off to a fast start but was chased and caught by Taylor who passed him to win in a personal best 9.94 seconds (0.1m/s). The Jamaican was second in 10.05 seconds, and South Africa’s Marko Ferreira took the bronze with 10.16 seconds.

Maxwell got the edge over Douglas at the start and held off the Jamaican to the tape, running 11.14 seconds (-0.1m/s), Douglas ran 11.17 seconds, with Italy’s Kelly Ann Maevane Doualla Edimo taking the bronze medal with 11.27 seconds.

Theianna-Lee Terrelonge was sixth in 11.37 seconds

Maxwell’s win was the first time in 10 years that an American took the women’s 100m and snapped the run by Jamaicans, who won the last four editions – Briana Williams in 2018, Tina Clayton in 2021 and 2022 and Alana Reid in 2024.

World.title: 92 NCU graduands initiated into nursing profession
World.content:
Sudane Spence (left) receives the top student awards for both the theoretical and clinical aspects of the four-year nursing degree programme at NCU during the Nurses’ Pinning and Thanksgiving Ceremony held August 5. She celebrates the moment with NCU Interim President Dr Vivienne Quarrie (centre) and keynote speaker Dr Nicola Brown, director of nursing services at the National Chest Hospital.

THE latest batch of nurses trained by Northern Caribbean University (NCU) was welcomed into the profession by Dr Nicola Brown, director of nursing services at the National Chest Hospital, who delivered the keynote address during the Nurses’ Pinning and Thanksgiving Service held on August 5 at the Mandeville-based institution.

The pinning ceremony marked the completion of four years of classroom instruction and clinical experience in the field by the nursing students.

Several practicing nurses participated in affixing pins to the graduands symbolising their initiation into the profession.

Dr Brown pointed out to the graduands that the pin represents a solemn covenant of service and responsibility and is a visible reminder that they are entering a profession “where knowledge meets humanity and skill meets compassion”.

Speaking on the theme ‘Transformed Minds, Compassionate Hearts for Christ-centred Service,’ Dr Brown highlighted several situations that the new nurses will face in delivering care.

She pointed out that these could include patients with “more complex health problems” which increasingly require mental health services and underscored that the new nurses will require the required knowledge, wisdom and situational awareness to provide appropriate patient care.

While noting the benefits of technology in delivering health care, Dr Brown warned against it becoming a barrier between the nurse and the “human being in the bed”.

The health administrator also advised the graduands to resist peer pressure in a working environment that tests their morale and professional ethics.

She argued that a transformed mind resists cynicism and refuses to become desensitised to the suffering of others, but instead recognises each patient as a person of inherent dignity, worthy of respect and compassionate care.

“Compassion bridges the gap between clinical competence and genuine care, making patients seen and valued,” said Dr Brown.

Turning to the prospect of burnout caused by nursing shortage and high turnover rates amid systemic pressures, Dr Brown advised the nurse graduands that in such moments it is their compassion that will sustain their calling.

She pointed to a link between compassion and Christ-centred service which is to embody love in action, demonstrating patience, kindness, humility, and grace in every interaction.

“Christ-centered service also requires integrity and courage in the face of challenges within health-care systems. It calls you to do what is right, even when no one is watching, and to advocate for those who cannot advocate for themselves,” added Dr Brown.

In her remarks to graduands, NCU Interim President Dr Vivienne Quarrie said nurses from the institution are recognised across Jamaica and the international community for their creativity, competence, and character.

She said their training was intentionally designed to transform their minds and shape compassionate hearts for service that reflects Christ-centred qualities.

“So, as you are pinned today, may you always remember that you were prepared to provide ethical service and to serve with unwavering moral commitment. Accordingly, may your transformed minds and compassionate hearts guide your practice, inspire your patients, and honour the one true God who has taken you to this point,” said Dr Quarrie.

Graduand Sudane Spence received the top student awards for both the theoretical and clinical aspects of the nursing degree programme.

Spence said she is eagerly looking forward to changing the lives of patients for the better using the knowledge and skills she and her fellow students gained over the four years of training at NCU.

The nurse graduands will participate in the NCU 103rd Commencement Ceremony to be held on Sunday.

World.title: Magyar’s party backs former supreme court head for Hungarian president
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s ruling Tisza party said on Saturday that it had nominated former Supreme Court President András Baka to become the country’s next president.

Baka, who worked as a judge on the European Court of Human Rights before being elected to head the Supreme Court, was removed from his post by the Fidesz government in 2011 — a move the ECHR ruled was unlawful.

“Throughout his career, Dr. András Baka has considered the principle of the separation of powers to be of paramount importance and has consistently stood up for the rule of law and judicial independence,” Tisza said in a Facebook post.

World.title: Sánchez-Meloni clash brings back borders — and headaches for tourists
World.content:
Madrid has pushed back forcefully against that narrative, and noted that the migrants could not leave the North African territory because they lack valid IDs required to travel on ferries to mainland Europe.

Spanish authorities and the European Commission this week confirmed that none of the 72,000 people who surged into Ceuta have crossed the Strait of Gibraltar. During a meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi publicly praised Spain for its handling of the situation and expressed Rome’s “sincere solidarity” with Madrid.

Yet despite requests from Madrid, the Italian government has declined to end border checks even after it became clear that there was no risk of the Ceuta crisis spilling into the rest of Europe. Rome’s inaction prompted Spain to issue a statement on Friday threatening to adopt “proportional measures” if Rome did not change course by Aug. 9.

After Meloni’s office responded by declaring “Italy does not accept ultimatums or demands from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Madrid moved to reintroduce its own controls.

Magnus Brunner, the European commissioner for internal affairs and migration, sought to mediate in the dispute.

“I was in contact with both the Spanish and Italian Interior Ministers today. Both confirmed that the internal border controls are temporary,” Brunner said in a post on X. “I stressed the progress we’ve made on tackling illegal migration and that trust between Member States is our most valuable currency.”

World.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 12, wound over 80 overnight
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the drone attacks killed three people — a 3-year-old child and the child’s grandparents — in a village in the Kyiv region. The six ballistic missiles struck civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, killing one person, he said.

“More pressure is needed. New sanctions that will prevent the production of these ballistic missiles,” Zelenskyy said on X. “And we definitely need more protection for our people,” he added, appealing to allies to provide missile interceptors to strengthen Ukraine’s defenses against Russia’s aerial assault.

In the Zaporizhzhia region, in southeast Ukraine, three people were killed and four were wounded following the overnight attack, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said.

A further five people were killed and nearly 50 people wounded in the regions of Kharkiv, Donetsk and Kherson, according to regional authorities.

Separately, Zelenskyy visited Serbia on Saturday — his first trip to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine — to meet with President Aleksandar Vučić and Prime Minister Đuro Macut.

Zelenskyy said the talks had focused on rebuilding infrastructure, readying a free-trade agreement this year, and preparing for the winter to come.

World.title: Gabriel Attal alleges Russian interference in French presidential race
World.content:
Gabriel Attal attends a session of questions to the government at the National Assembly, in Paris on January 6, 2026. | Christophe Petit Tesson/EPA

Attal becomes the latest contender to file a complaint over alleged Russian interference ahead of the April 2027 presidential vote.

Former prime minister and presidential candidate Gabriel Attal has filed a complaint over an alleged Russian disinformation campaign ahead of next year’s French presidential election, local news outlets reported on Saturday.

Attal’s lawyers told French media that the complaint, filed on Friday, denounces “acts of foreign interference, manipulation of information, fabrication of content likely to undermine the fundamental interests of the nation and the sincerity of the upcoming presidential election.”

They told BFMTV that several accounts on social network X, some of which impersonated French and international media, had disseminated fake video reports and newspaper articles attributing false statements to Attal that were “intended to discredit him as a candidate.”

World.title: Germany’s gas gamble puts Europe’s winter at risk
World.content:
The low reserves have already added to the increased pressure on gas prices linked to renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, with the European natural gas benchmark now consistently higher than it was for the first four months of the Iran war.

The European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, has said the bloc faces no winter supply risks. But a report by energy analytics firm Rapidan projects that reserves will rise to only 65 percent of total storage capacity by November, arguing that hitting the EU's target by winter won't be possible without "materially higher prices."

That risk has been exacerbated, analysts say, by the bloc’s move in recent years to replace its long-term supply deals with Russia with short-term purchases of globally traded liquefied natural gas. These seaborne cargoes are highly mobile and go to the highest bidder — leaving buyers more exposed to volatility on international markets, especially in the wake of the loss of key supplies from Qatar and rising demand in Asia.

A tanker passes through the Strait of Hormuz on Feb. 25, 2026. | Fadel Senna/AFP via Getty Images

Germany, the bloc's largest gas consumer, has seen its reserves fill up even more slowly than others, in part thanks to its more hands-off, market-led approach to restocking than many of its neighbors. As a result, reserves stood at only 47 percent of national capacity in August, according to the latest data — the lowest fill level since records began. That's especially worrying as the country's reserves are important for the bloc as a whole, representing over 20 percent of the EU's storage capacity.

Nevertheless, Berlin is staying the course. While its energy ministry has acknowledged the country's historically low reserves, it has refused to intervene to direct its main state-controlled gas buyers, SEFE and Uniper, to buy gas at current prices to ensure its targets are met, instead of waiting for market conditions to improve.

"It is the responsibility of companies and traders to fill the storage facilities for the winter," a spokesperson for the German energy ministry told POLITICO. "Government-led filling of the storage facilities would further constrain the gas market and drive prices even higher. The supply situation over the coming months would actually deteriorate."

World.title: Italy says it won’t take orders from Spain on border checks
World.content:
Earlier in the day, the Spanish government had threatened to take “proportional measures” if Rome did not stop its reintroduced border checks and temporary suspension of the Schengen Agreement by Aug. 9.

In its statement, Rome said it would keep these controls in place “at least until August 15 and, in any case, until security and terrorism risks to Italy can be completely ruled out,” adding that a new “migratory wave” is expected in Ceuta on that date.

“Only when it is certain that there will be no security or terrorism risks for Italy, that there will be no new wave and that there are no irregular migrants heading toward European territory will it be possible to reconsider what has already been decided,” said the document.

World.title: EU adds 5 people to Russia sanctions list after latest deadly attacks on Ukraine
World.content:
Russia this week carried out one of its deadliest barrages on Kyiv, killing 17.

The EU has added five individuals to its Russia sanctions list. The move was driven by Moscow’s “intensified strikes deliberately targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure” in Ukraine, according to a press release.

The press release does not refer to a specific attack, but earlier this week Russia carried out one of its deadliest barrages on the Ukrainian capital, killing 17. In July, a similar attack in Kyiv killed 12.

Among those included in the new sanctions is Ramil Badgutdinov — the head of a company that helps produce the Iskander-M ballistic missiles — and Aleksandr Dyukarev, head of the KrasMash plant that produces Sarmat ballistic missiles. Russia has not yet used Sarmat missiles in Ukraine, but Moscow has been testing them.

World.title: Two drones spottled flying over military base in the western part of the country, German armed forces say
World.content:
Two drones were spotted flying over a German military base in the western part of the country, just two days after a drone carrying explosives was found at a key cargo airport, the German Armed Forces said in a statement on Saturday.

 

Security surveillance at the Bundeswehr base in Mechernich reported seeing two drones around 10 pm on Thursday, according to a statement from the German Joint Force Command. The sightings were confirmed and military police forces were deployed to the site.

The military said the Euskirchen police department has opened an investigation. The police did not immediately respond to a request for comment and the military did not release additional details.

Recently, drone sightings over civilian and cargo airports have been more widely reported.

'New quality of danger'

Last year, mysterious drone flights over the airspace of European Union member countries alarmed the public and authorities, and also prompted the cancellation of dozens of flights that stranded thousands of passengers at several major airports from Copenhagen to Warsaw.

Thursday's sighting of the two drones came after a drone with explosives was found at Germany’s Leipzig-Halle Airport shortly before midnight on Tuesday. The device and its detonator were destroyed in a controlled explosion, with German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt calling the incident a “new quality of danger.”

Leipzig-Halle is a major hub for international freight and for providing support to Ukraine. Since Russia’s war on Ukraine broke out in February 2022, it has also doubled as a base for Kyiv’s national cargo carrier, Antonov Airlines.

It is also home to NATO’s Strategic Airlift International Solution, or SALIS, which is currently operational almost every day in delivering equipment to NATO battle groups along its eastern flank from Finland to Romania and supporting EU and alliance nation missions.

In 2024, an incendiary device ignited at a logistics centre at the airport and set fire to a freight container, part of a plot that Western security officials suspect was organized by Russian intelligence.

Western officials have accused Russia and its proxies of staging dozens of attacks and other incidents across Europe since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The Russian Embassy in Germany on Friday called the Leipzig drone incident part of a “new wave of anti-Russian hysteria in Germany.”

World.title: Wedding at Funchal cathedral, but not Cristiano and Georgina's, to the disappointment of hundreds
World.content:
At around three o'clock on Saturday afternoon, hundreds of people began to gather outside Funchal's Sé Cathedral in Madeira. The ceremony was running slightly late: the bride was missing, the last to arrive, as is customary.

 

Outside, around two thousand people with their mobile phones held aloft tried to capture the precious moment; many will have managed it, but when they realised that the bride was not Georgina Rodriguez but Nicole, and those who did get into the church saw that it was not Ronaldo standing by the altar but Fábio, they will surely have been left disappointed.

For this expat couple now living in France, it will have been a particularly lively ceremony. "We feel like celebrities," one of the guests joked to the Diário de Notícias da Madeira (source in Portuguese).

Some people travelled to Madeira especially to attend what would have been the most talked-about wedding of the year, if the rumour spread by the British tabloids had been confirmed.

That was the case for the eldest daughter of Helena Ferro Gouveia, a former journalist and commentator on CNN Portugal, who said her eldest, a "die-hard fan" of Cristiano, travelled specially from Germany to "catch a glimpse of the wedding" of Diogo and Nicole.

For now, however, the details of the nuptials remain nothing more than rumours fuelled by the national and international celebrity press. Imagination is not in short supply, with some outlets even providing details of an entirely fictitious ceremony.

Last week the press was adamant that Cris and Gio were going to get married at the Quinta da Regaleira in Sintra on Saturday, 2 August. This week, The Sun wrote that the ceremony would take place on 8 August at Funchal Cathedral, at 3 pm, and that the reception would be held at the Savoy Palace hotel, having discovered that on that very day the luxury hotel had reserved two floors for a private event.

The pressure from the international media has been so intense that the Funchal diocese decided to publish images of Saturday's wedding between Fábio and Nicole to help clear the churchyard.

"After a lot of confusion in the street with so many journalists and tourists, we finally managed to close the church and celebrate," the diocese wrote in a post shared on Facebook.

The rumours keep on gathering strength, especially on social media, where the famous couple has been betrothed time and time again. There are even AI-doctored photos and videos of the ceremony showing star guests such as Yamine Lamal, Mbappé, Messi and Neymar.

But it is also on social media that the rumours lose traction, particularly if you pay attention to the posts from the people closest to Cristiano.

Take his sister, Kátia Aveiro, for example, who this morning posted on Instagram saying that she was in Lisbon and would be staying in the Portuguese capital "for a few more days". Hard to imagine she would want to miss her brother's wedding.

World.title: Major wildfire in hills above Lake Garda: at least 200 residents and tourists evacuated
World.content:
A major wildfire broke out on Friday evening in Alto Garda, in the Tignale mountains on the western shore of Lake Garda. Firefighters, civil protection teams, forest Carabinieri and volunteer fire crews are on site working to secure the area. The response is being coordinated by the mayor of Tignale, Daniele Bonassi, who described the scenes as "terrifying".

 

The blaze has not yet been brought under control because of winds of up to 40 kilometres an hour, which are rapidly changing the direction of the flames. The area has been hit hard by the drought of recent weeks, leaving vegetation dry and highly vulnerable to fire. This morning two Canadair water-bombing aircraft were also deployed to try to stop the flames.

Wildfire in Tignale, firefighters in action Vigili del Fuoco

The authorities have ordered the evacuation of 200 people. Overnight, guests were moved out of holiday homes and the "La Forca" residence, which hosts many Italian and foreign tourists. Rescuers are going house to housebecause it is sometimes unclear which properties are currently occupied or used by tourists. So far, no injuries have been reported.

The cause of the blaze is still unclear, and for now rescue efforts are focused on containing the flames.

World.title: Serbia's Vučić sends signal to Brussels and Moscow by hosting Zelenskyy with pomp and circumstance
World.content:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić said he hopes to see an end to the war in Ukraine, but doubts it will happen soon.

 

"If you ask me, and as a political veteran, I can tell you that I’m not sure about it, and I’m very much afraid that we’ll have another difficult winter," Vučić said during a joint press briefing with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who is visiting Belgrade.

“But I just hope, without any real facts behind these hopes, that this will end tomorrow," he added.

Zelenskyy arrived to Belgrade on Friday for his first official visit to Serbia since becoming president in 2019.

The Ukrainian president received an honour guard welcome on Saturday, followed by a meeting at the Presidential Palace with his Serbian counterpart.

As part of the visit, the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture and the Ukrainian Ambassador to Serbia signed a Memorandum of Understanding.

Following the bilateral signing, Vučić said the two nations will soon deliver a free trade deal, saying it is of "utmost importance for our country and Ukraine".

"We will work hard and I believe that swiftly and efficiently we will deliver it to our people," Vučić added.

While Ukraine seeks to strengthen international support amid Russia’s ongoing and intensifying strikes, Belgrade is seeking to balance this relationship with Moscow against pressure from the European Union to align with the bloc’s foreign policy.

By hosting Zelenskyy, Vučić is sending a strong signal to the EU, but also to Russia.

Serbia is one of the few European countries that has kept close ties with Moscow following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, relying almost entirely on Russia for its energy supplies.

Prior to the meeting with Zelenskyy, Vučić reiterated Belgrade's stance that it would not impose tougher sanctions on Russia. Serbia, however, has provided aid to Ukraine in the form of direct financial and humanitarian assistance, though not military.

Zelenskyy: Weapon agreements are in place, but supplies remain insufficient

Zelenskyy’s visit to Serbia comes as Moscow continues its strikes on Ukraine. Overnight, Russian forces launched several attacks on Kyiv, killing at least three people, including a child, and injuring several others.

Russia has significantly intensified its attacks on the Ukrainian capital in recent months, often by firing ballistic missiles that are difficult to intercept.

"There was another missile strike last night—ballistic missiles targeting our infrastructure. There were also attack drones. In particular, reactive Shahed drones were again targeting our energy facilities and railways," Zelenskyy said during the joint press conference with Vučić.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy with Serbian counterpart Aleksandar Vučić during welcome ceremony at the Serbia Palace, in Belgrade, Serbia, Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic

Speaking on Ukraine's defence against Russian aggression, the Ukrainian leader said there are agreements in place for weapon distribution, but supply has not been sufficient.

"Who has ballistic missiles and systems? The manufacturer. That’s the United States of America, first and foremost. Can they help? We’re working on this. Will they provide us with missiles every month? Yes, we have agreements in place. But are these missiles enough? No," Zelenskyy said.

Several US media reported about Washington's dwindling weapons stockpile, claims that President Donald Trump has denied.

Zelenskyy said that supplies of air defence systems from foreign partners decreased in 2026 compared to last year, and called on Europe to contribute more.

"We say the Americans have to provide them, but the Europeans too—we’re working it out with them. The process for some of these licenses is also taking a long time. And that’s the truth," the Ukrainian president said.

World.title: Belarus joins Russia’s war on freedom of information
World.content:
Belarus' decision to ban the Euronews website by designating it as “extremist” and adding it to its “Republican List of Extremist Materials” marks a new escalation by authorities in Minsk in their crackdown on independent media and free speech.

 

The Belarus Ministry of Information’s move, reported by Belarus-based media, resulted in the immediate restriction of access to Euronews’ digital platforms in the country’s territory, as shown by Euronews’ real-time traffic-monitoring systems.

As of Saturday, Belarus has still not communicated its decision to Euronews, which was reportedly taken on 4 August - nor has it outlined the reasoning behind it.

The Ministry of Information had already banned Euronews’ television broadcasts in April 2021 following its coverage of nationwide protests against Belarusian leader Aliaksandr Lukashenka.

Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko speaks to journalists during a joint press conference with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at Merdeka Palace in Jakarta. AP Photo

The Belarus government's official argument then was that Euronews’ broadcasting license had expired and that the channel was publishing adverts in English rather than translating them into Russian or Belarusian in line with local laws.

Euronews was also not notified of that decision and once again learned of the ban through media outlets in Belarus.

In a statement published after the 2021 ban came into effect, Euronews condemned the decision and said that it would "do its utmost to ensure that its audiences in Belarus can very soon again have access, on television, to its hallmark impartial and quality journalism."

"In the meantime, these audiences will be able to continue following us on our digital platforms," it added.

Following in Russia's footsteps

Euronews had built a significant audience in Belarus and in Russia over the years, its digital traffic data shows.

However, Moscow decided to ban Euronews’ television and digital platforms across Russia in March 2022, shortly after it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, as Euronews refused to comply with the censorship and propaganda-driven measures imposed by the Kremlin on the media.

Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister - Presidential Envoy to the Far Eastern Federal District Yury Trutnev at the Kremlin in Moscow. Sputnik

The decision to stop broadcasting Euronews was taken by Russia’s audio-visual regulator Roskomnadzor following a request from the Prosecutor General’s Office. It threatened Euronews with “criminal liability” and accused the outlet of publishing “unreliable information on a special military operation being carried out by the Russian Armed Forces, as well as information containing calls for people to participate in mass (public) events.”

After Russian President Vladimir Putin's troops invaded Ukraine, the Kremlin told the media not to call its full-scale invasion a war, while also issuing other directives that contravened Euronews’ fundamental editorial values.

Responding at the time, Euronews rejected “the allegations of 'fake news' and of calling citizens to protest”.

“We firmly condemn this intolerable restriction imposed on the millions of people across Russia who relied on Euronews, more than ever, to get impartial fact-based news, in a context of heightened disinformation and propaganda,” Euronews said in a statement.

Russian authorities continued to criminalise the dissemination of what it called information “discrediting” the Russian army and threatened journalists with up to 15 years in prison.

More recently, Euronews revealed that multiple fake news videos were being posted on Russian social media copying the publication's journalistic and visual style in an attempt to spread false political information.

These come as part of a wider, sophisticated fake news campaign targeting Western media and European societies.

Belarus, Russia and Iran’s media crackdown

Minsk's decision mirrors a series of similar measures taken by Moscow in clamping down on internet platforms it does not fully control.

On the same day that Belarus took the decision to ban Euronews’ digital platforms, the Kremlin blocked dozens of VPN services used by Russians to bypass internet restrictions in a move that experts described as one of the largest crackdowns on VPN services in recent years.

The latest VPN blockade comes as Russia has been imposing constant restrictions on media outlets, social media and foreign technology companies ever since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In July 2025, Russia imposed a new legislation criminalising "searching for extremist content online", marking the first time Moscow hit internet users for consuming and distributing content deemed as banned in further crackdown on dissent and independent journalism.

Belarus’ decision to classify Euronews’ journalism as “extremist” appears to match this Russian legislation.

Then in August 2025, Russian authorities announced they were “partially” restricting calls through Telegram and WhatsApp messaging applications, in a further effort to tighten control over the internet and since the beginning of 2026 the Kremlin moved to fully block Telegram and WhatsApp everywhere across the country, triggering the largest wave of criticism from Kremlin supporters against the authorities in four years since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The Iranian regime followed Russia and Belarus’ method to eliminate any outside information reaching their societies by bluntly blocking all internet access across Iran when it cracked down on the massive anti-regime protests in January 2026 and continued maintaining the internet ban throughout the Iran war.

Over the last months, the Tehran regime also imposed further measures of internet control and severe penalties on VPN usage, while designating selected medias as enemies of the state.

World.title: Tisza Party group nominates András Baka for new Hungarian president
World.content:
András Baka is an internationally recognised legal scholar, who began his career at the Institute for Legal Studies of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, then became director general of the College of Public Administration. The peak of his international judicial career came when he served for two terms, between 1991 and 2008, as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) in Strasbourg. On his return home, in 2009, parliament elected him president of the Supreme Court. The second Orbán government, which came to power in 2010 with a constitution-making majority, removed him by renaming the Supreme Court as the Curia, thereby formally creating a new institution and appointing a new head to lead it.

 

Baka subsequently won a case against the Hungarian state at the European Court of Human Rights, which found that his rights to a fair trial and to freedom of expression had been violated. He has been a regular voice on rule-of-law issues in Hungary and abroad. He is an independent-minded, somewhat old-school lawyer, and Hungary has had several presidents of this type. His ability to embody national unity may be complicated by the fact that he has been an outspoken critic of the Orbán system both at home and internationally.

Powerless presidents instead of symbols of national unity

Before the elections, Tisza Party leader Péter Magyar had already indicated that, if they secured a constitution-making majority, they would remove most of the high public dignitaries appointed by Fidesz, with the exception of central bank governor Mihály Varga. He argued that these dignitaries were loyal Fidesz party foot soldiers who had failed to fulfil their constitutional duties and whose aim after the election would be to obstruct the work of the Tisza government.

In the Hungarian system the president of the republic primarily plays a ceremonial role and has little independent political room for manoeuvre. Under Fidesz rule, however, the presidents did not use even this limited legal and communicative space, instead operating in parallel with the government and cooperating with it in every respect.

During the period of government from 2010 to 2016, only János Áder, a political veteran of the party, managed to serve the two terms available to him in full.

László Sólyom, who had been elevated to the post by Fidesz while it was still in opposition and who projected an independent political and legal profile, was not elected for a second term. His successor, Pál Schmitt, a former Fidesz vice president, fell over a plagiarism scandal. János Áder then became president, and after his second term he was followed by Katalin Novák.

Novák spent her entire political career in Fidesz, but as a young woman she was officially meant to show a more European, more Western-facing face of the party than the mainstream led by Viktor Orbán. She had to step down after the pardon for sex abuse scandal. At that point Tamás Sulyok was elected, a figure little known to the public and without a strong public profile, and he too did not complete his first term.

President Tamás Sulyok was ultimately removed by means of a short sentence inserted into the 17th constitutional amendment, which the lawyer elected by Fidesz signed, thereby ending his mandate.

Tisza has indicated that it will adopt a new constitution within this parliamentary term and will at least consider the possibility of electing the president of the republic directly.

Tisza's first political misstep

Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised public consultation on the choice of president, then, after a very short time, announced that the parliamentary group was nominating women's world chess champion Judit Polgár. The announcement was followed by a strong outcry; critics of the decision argued that the absence of consultation cast a shadow over the selection process. Sensing the outrage, Polgár declined Magyar's offer. After the failed nomination, Medián, one of Hungary's most trusted pollsters, measured the first significant drop (3–5 percentage points) in support for Tisza, which nevertheless remained at a historically high level, at 68% among decided party voters.

Tisza chose Baka from three candidates; the other two were historian Ignác Romsics and independent lawyer Botond Fülöp, who publishes under the pseudonym Vidéki Prókátor and was the one who brought to light the pardon case that led to President Katalin Novák's resignation.

World.title: Turkey's new opposition party offers hope, but its future is already in jeopardy
World.content:
The launch of the Yeni Party in Turkey promises to energise the country's struggling opposition. But while some polls show it leading, it remains vulnerable – already beset by arrests it says are "politically motivated".

Advertising

In a glitzy video, set to pumping music and shared widely across social media, Ozgur Ozel launched the Yeni Party – "New Party" – vowing to usher in a new era in Turkish politics and end President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s long rule.

Ozel founded the New Party after a court removed him from leading the main opposition party, the Republican People’s Party (CHP).

His rival, former party leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu, 77, who lost every election during his decade in charge of the CHP, replaced him.

Many in the country believe Erdogan played a role in the removal of Ozel, as his popularity grew thanks to tireless campaigning.

Riding the wave

The New Party is settings its sights beyond the CHP’s usual supporters.

"It covers the whole political spectrum in Turkish political life," explains Ozel's advisor Ilham Uzel.

"There are critical elements like democratisation, rule of law, secularism and a pro-Western approach, so we maintain these main pillars. But it is not confined to social democracy; we reach out to every section of Turkish society, including Islamists and conservatives, nationalists and liberals. We have Kurdish supporters."

The New Party is riding a wave of excitement. Ninety-one out of 135 CHP parliamentary deputies have defected to its ranks, joined by dozens of mayors and it is swiftly becoming the main opposition in parliament.

Turkey opposition worries that Europe is sacrificing democracy for security

Some polls show the party soaring above 30 percent, leaving Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party behind, while the CHP’s support has collapsed.

The New Party’s broad approach is finding fertile ground. "Even those who still support the governing coalition, the AK Party and MHP, are unhappy with how things are or how politics is practised, especially regarding economic issues. So there is a push towards change," says political commentator Sezin Oney.

"There is a yearning to change things at the grassroots, and the New Party may be the only party that can represent a new way of doing politics. But they have to live up to it, of course."

Corruption charges

Erdogan has remained in power for more than 20 years partly by exploiting divisions within the opposition, which is made up of conservatives, hardline secularists, and both Kurdish and Turkish nationalists.

The New Party has a key advantage over the strongly secular CHP, whose history is linked to past policies targeting Turkey’s large Kurdish minority and religious conservatives.

"CHP is identified with many bad experiences that the Kurds and conservative people had in past decades," said Mesut Yegen of the Diyarbakir-based Kurdish Studies Center.

"If you look at what Ozgur Ozel says during his speeches, you may clearly see the Yeni Party doesn’t have the baggage of CHP."

Erdogan has also often exploited the CHP’s history, painting it as anti-religious and hostile to Kurdish minority rights. The New Party faces the tricky task of keeping CHP loyalists on board while reaching new supporters.

But for now, simply staying out of jail may be the most pressing concern for its representatives.

Turkey marks a decade since the coup that never was, but never really ended

Several mayors who joined the New Party have been arrested on corruption charges, widely seen as politically motivated. In the past two years, 26 opposition mayors and hundreds of officials have been imprisoned on corruption allegations, compared to two mayors from Erdogan’s AK Party.

"They are cracking down on our party – every other day, mayors are arrested," says Uzgel. "They filed another charge against our leader. Nobody is safe in this authoritarian regime. So Mr Ozel is on the spot, definitely."

Ozel is protected by parliamentary immunity, but Oney warns he may be running out of time.

"Ozgur Ozel might be imprisoned himself once his immunity is removed by a parliamentary vote, that's a possibility. The only immunity he can have is the immunity bestowed upon him by the people. So only public opinion is protecting him. How much can it protect him? We'll see."

With parliament about to break for summer until October, Ozel has a brief window to strengthen his party and rally public support.

World.title: Canada: British Columbia declares emergency as fires spread
World.content:
More than 20,000 people have been forced from their homes by out-of-control wildfires in Canada's British Columbia, where 105 blazes are currently burning.

Canadian officials on Saturday declared a state of emergency in British Columbia after more than 20,000 people were ordered to flee a fast-moving wildfire.

Describing the intensity of the blaze, British Columbia Premier David Eby said a fire official compared it to "a bomb going off."

"He described flames on a 100-foot (30-meter) tree, flames going 200 feet above that, and the fire creating its own weather system, which creates lightning," Eby said.

"Homes have been lost, and properties have been destroyed. Some people became trapped as conditions changed very quickly, and needed to be rescued," he added.

Wildfire in British Columbia nearly doubles in size overnight

The fire, first reported Friday evening, grew rapidly overnight, triggering widespread evacuation orders.

By Saturday, it had spread to about 9,500 hectares (23,500 acres), prompting all 12,000 residents of the Summerland district to evacuate.

The Summerland blaze is one of many fires challenging emergency crews across British Columbia.

The province has seen 70 new wildfires over the past week, and 105 are currently burning, according to British Columbia Minister of Forests Ravi Parmar.

A dry and hot summer has ⁠led to more than ​4,500 fires in Canada this year [FILE: August 3, 2026] Image: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/picture alliance

Canada grapples with large wildfires

Fires have scorched 4 million hectares in Canada in 2026, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Center .

Blazes flared up in several regions, including Ontario and Quebec, this year as hot, dry conditions fueled fires in dense forest areas.

In recent years, Canada has faced a growing number of destructive wildfire seasons.

World.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
World.content:
Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

FIFA warned against what it calls a "concerted and ongoing effort" to "undermine" the organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

The statement, issued late on Saturday, comes amid a growing dispute over Infantino's leadership after the failed plan to create a subsidiary to run the men's World Cup and other events, with up to a 20% stake offered to external investors.

The proposal drew criticism from European governing body UEFA, which threatened to boycott future World Cups, as well as several national associations and senior FIFA officials, and prompted calls for Infantino to resign.

Amid the growing criticism Infantino persuaded FIFA's Board of Management to express its full support for him at a crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco, on Wednesday.

FIFA accused of blackmail in exchange for Infantino support To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Report raises new questions over Infantino

The pressure on Infantino intensified on Friday when British newspaper the Daily Telegraph reported a six-figure sum was paid to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with him during his time as UEFA general secretary.

UEFA confirmed a departure payment and said it also funded her MBA course, stating both were in line with regulations at the time.

A FIFA spokesman told the Telegraph on Friday: "FIFA president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue."

Responding to the latest scrutiny, FIFA said on Saturday, without directly mentioning the Telegraph report, "recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its President."

Investment plan dispute deepens leadership crisis

The fallout over the shelved private investment plan has overshadowed Infantino's bid for a fourth term as FIFA president.

After this week's crisis meeting, UEFA said it no longer has confidence in him, and Norwegian FA President Lise Klaveness called for his resignation.

Despite the controversy, Infantino retains strong backing among FIFA members, with the Confederation of African Football (CAF) unanimously supporting his leadership and South American governing body CONMEBOL opposing any attempt to remove him without a vote of all member associations.

FIFA said that those who lacked the support of its member associations should not seek to achieve "allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes."

World.title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
World.content:
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt on Sunday warned that hybrid warfare attacks had become a daily threat to the country.

"We're not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare," Dobrindt told the newspaper Bild am Sonntag following the discovery of a drone carrying explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

"Espionage, sabotage, cyberattacks, or covert operations by foreign powers aimed at destabilizing Germany or inflicting direct harm are a constant reality," Dobrindt said.

He also noted that the country is stepping up research into drones to address new security threats.

A new drone security research center will be established later in August at a German Aerospace Center (DLR) test airport in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, Dobrindt said.

Drone warfare: German startup draws on Ukraine's experience To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Drones spotted above military base in west Germany

On Saturday, Germany's armed forces confirmed that two drones had been spotted late on Thursday over a German military base in Mechernich in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia near the Belgian border.

The drones were detected at around 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) over the Bundeswehr base, a German armed forces spokesperson said.

German media reported that the base hosts personnel responsible for the maintenance of US Patriot air defense systems, which play a key role in defending Ukraine against Russian aerial attacks.

Drone incident at Leipzig airport

The sighting in Mechernich comes just two days after the discovery of a drone carrying explosives a Ukrainian transport plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport, an incident Dobrindt called a "hybrid attack scenario."

While German government officials have refrained from publicly blaming any foreign country over the Leipzig incident, some lawmakers have pointed fingers at Russia, which has been at war with Ukraine since ​its full-scale invasion of the country in 2022.

On Friday, the Russian Embassy in Berlin dismissed the Leipzig event as a "fabricated provocation" and said Russia was once more being accused of hostile actions "without the slightest evidence being presented."

World.title: Nigeria marries 1,500 couples in mass wedding
World.content:
The government describes the program as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability. Among those married were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

Some 1,500 couples got married at a mass wedding organized by Abba Kabir Yusuf, the governor of Kano state, in northern Nigeria.

The regional government described the two-day event as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability.

"The whole idea for the marriage is to help our families and we husbands who are not financially stable to marry; that's why the government is helping us get married," groom Abubakar Aliyu Musa told the Associated Press.

This is the second time Yusuf's administration has organized a mass wedding.

The two-day ceremony was held in northern Kano state Image: Sani Maikatanga/AP Photo/picture alliance

What else do we know about the program in Kano state?

According to Kano's regional government, each bride received a dowry of 200,000 naira ($147, €127) and support to set up a small business.

The couples were also given household items including beds, mattresses and blankets.

The couples underwent screening and counseling before the wedding.

Governor Yusuf described the program as a "bold social intervention aimed at restoring hope and supporting dignified family life in Kano."

"The program was designed not only to assist women who might otherwise struggle to afford marriage, but also to strengthen families and promote social stability in the state," he said.

Widower remarries in mass wedding

Among those who participated in the mass wedding were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

One of them was Haruna Bashir, who lost his wife and six children in an attack earlier in the year. Daurawa hailed the ceremony as a step toward Bashir "gradually returning to normal life" after having "hardly interacted with people … since the tragic incident."

Nigeria has been grappling with a major security crisis for years, particularly in the country's north, which is regularly hit by raids and attacks by Islamist insurgents and organized gangs.

Many armed groups in Nigeria also kidnap schoolchildren to demand large ransoms.

On Wednesday, the Nigerian government announced the release of 308 people who had been abducted.
